statement: Torsion in an acting group and its action on torsion are different assertions Lochak and Schneps (1997, Proposition 4(i)) prove \(C_F(c)=1\); Proposition 4(ii) proves that \(c\) is self-centralizing in \(\widehat{GT}\). Schneps (1997, \S1.4(4)) and Lochak and Schneps (2006, Question 1.4) ask whether all nonidentity torsion in \(\widehat{GT}\) consists of conjugates of \(c\). Harbater and Schneps (2000, Main Theorem(a), proved by Propositions 3--4 and Theorem 2) identify \(\widehat{GT}_0\) with the centralizer in \(\mathcal P\) of the geometric \(S_3\). Collas's genus-zero Theorems 3.3 and 3.10 identify prime-order torsion in \(\widehat\Gamma_{0,[n]}\) with discrete torsion and prove the \(\lambda\)-conjugacy action of \(\widehat{GT}\). His genus-one Theorems 6.3 and 6.5 give the corresponding statements with acting group \(\widehat{GR}\), isomorphic to the subgroup denoted \(I\Gamma\) in that article; replacing it there by all of \(\widehat{GT}\) is not justified by those theorems.\cite{A_LS1997,A_Schneps1997,A_LS2006,A_HS2000,A_Collas2012a,A_Collas2012b}
notes: Known results concern specified acting groups and targets; not a solution of torsion in GT.

statement: Relative pronilpotent levels recover the full peripheral group For an open characteristic subgroup \(U\) of \(F\), put \[ R_U=R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U),\quad F_U=F/R_U,\quad P_U=\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F_U). \] For \(V\subset U\), the quotient \(F_V\to F_U\) induces a continuous epimorphism \(P_V\to P_U\). There is an isomorphism of profinite groups \[ \mathcal P \xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_U P_U. \] Two elements of \(\mathcal P\) are conjugate in \(\mathcal P\) if and only if their images are conjugate in every \(P_U\). This proves Lead 1.
notes: All transition maps typed; conjugacy detection uses compact transporter sets.

statement: A central quotient is the exact obstruction to a peripheral lift Let \(N\) be a closed characteristic subgroup of \(F\), and let \([N,F]\) denote the closed subgroup generated by commutators between \(N\) and \(F\). An automorphism \(a\) of \(F/N\), with specified conjugators \(b_i\) satisfying \[ a(\bar x_i)=b_i\bar x_i b_i^{-1},\qquad (x_1,x_2,x_3)=(x,y,z), \] lifts to a peripheral automorphism of \(F\) with these conjugators if and only if it lifts to a peripheral \emph{automorphism} of \(F/[N,F]\) with conjugators above the \(b_i\). This proves Lead 2.
notes: Central quotient lift must itself be an automorphism; no equivariant lift inferred.

statement: A degree-three coefficient imposed by the third cusp Over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero or greater than three, use the free class-three Lie algebra on \(X,Y\), and set \[ Z=[X,Y],\quad U_3=[X,Z],\quad V_3=[Y,Z],\quad x=\exp X,\quad y=\exp Y . \] If \(x\mapsto x^\mu,\ y\mapsto g^{-1}y^\mu g\), with \(\mu\in k^\times\) and \(\log g=tZ+\text{central terms}\), sends \(xy\) to a conjugate of \((xy)^\mu\), then \(t=(\mu^2-1)/24\).
notes: Necessary coefficient t=(mu^2-1)/24, proved directly.

statement: The specified conjugator in task A.3 need not preserve the third cusp There is an involution \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\), conjugate to \(c\) by a Galois element, for which the unique solution \(h\in F'\) of \(f_\alpha=h^{-1}\alpha(h)\) gives \[ \psi(x)=x,\qquad\psi(y)=hyh^{-1} \] that does not preserve the conjugacy class of \(z\) on \(F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(F)\). The failure occurs in the class-three exponent-seven quotient of order \(7^5\).
notes: Finite certificate order16807; actual example alpha=theta c theta^-1 in Galois image.

statement: The pure centralizer of standard conjugation has two elements \[ C_{\mathcal P}(c)=N_{\mathcal P}(\langle c\rangle)=\{1,c\}. \] If \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}_0\), every conjugator in \(\mathcal P\) from \(c\) to \(\alpha\) belongs to \(\widehat{GT}_0\).
answers: Task A.3; Task A.8; LM4 D.49
notes: Reproof of unrefereed LM4 D.49 core assertion.

statement: The multiplier-one cohomology set already has continuum many classes For \(G=\mathcal P,\widehat{GT}_0\), or \(\widehat{GT}\), put \(H_G=\ker\lambda\), with \(C_2\) acting by \(c\). There is a canonical closed injection of profinite spaces \[ \widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}/\{1,-1\} \longrightarrow H^1(C_2,H_G),\qquad \mu\longmapsto[\theta_\mu c\theta_\mu^{-1}c], \] where \(\theta_\mu\) is any element of multiplier \(\mu\). The set \(H^1(C_2,H_G)\) has cardinality \(2^{\aleph_0}\). For \(G=\widehat{GT}_0\), \(\Delta\) vanishes on this closed family. All these \(H_G\)-conjugacy classes form one \(G\)-conjugacy class.
notes: Canonical closed standard family; cardinality continuum; Delta zero there.

statement: Full conjugacy is an additional quotient of nonabelian cohomology With the notation of A.7, the full \(G\)-conjugacy classes of nonidentity involutions are \[ \widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\backslash H^1(C_2,H_G). \] The action of \(\mu\), using any lift \(\theta_\mu\), is \[ [a]\longmapsto[\,\theta_\mu a\,c(\theta_\mu^{-1})\,]. \] For \(\mathcal N=\ker(\mathcal P\to P_F)\), the \(\mathcal N\)-conjugacy classes of involutions with image exactly \(c_F\) are \(H^1(C_2,\mathcal N)\). Full \(\mathcal P\)-conjugacy on that fibre further quotients by \(C_{P_F}(c_F)\), acting by lifted conjugation, which need not preserve the distinguished cohomology class.
answers: Task A.3; Task A.5; Task A.8
notes: Correct full-conjugacy quotient; multiplier action can move distinguished point.

statement: Odd-prime conjugacy over a relative Frattini level Let \(U\) be open characteristic in \(F\), let \(p\) be odd, put \(E_p=F/O^p(U)\), \(V=U/O^p(U)\), and consider the peripheral outer subgroup preserving \(V\). Its kernel on \[ E_p/\Phi(V)=F/\overline{U'U^p} \] is pro-\(p\). Two involutions with the same image in this Frattini quotient are conjugate by the kernel. This applies to the fibre over \(c\), where that fibre is defined by descent to \(F/U\).
notes: Preservation of U^(p) typed explicitly; automatically holds for fully characteristic U.

statement: Every negative pure pro-\(p\) involution is locally conjugate for odd \(p\) Let \(P^{(p)}\) be the pure peripheral outer group of \(F^{(p)}\), with multiplier in \(\mathbb Z_p^\times\), for odd \(p\). Every involution of multiplier \(-1\) is conjugate to \(c\) by a multiplier-one element.
notes: Some local multiplier-one conjugator exists, not necessarily the specified h.

statement: A peripheral reflection triangle is equivalent to full conjugacy For a nontrivial involution \(\alpha\in\mathcal P\) let \(E=F\rtimes_\alpha C_2\). Then \(\alpha\) is conjugate to \(c\) in \(\mathcal P\) exactly when there are involutions \(t_0,t_1,t_2\) representing its three section classes such that \[ a=t_1t_0,\qquad b=t_0t_2,\qquad d=t_2t_1 \] generate conjugates of the respective inertia groups of \(x,y,z\), and the \(t_i\) generate \(E\) topologically. The last condition is equivalent to generation in every \(E/R_U\).
notes: Cote145 scan23 product-order convention made explicit.

statement: Dyadic and mixed-prime involution obstructions A.9 does not determine all two-primary classes or all gluing classes over \(U=F'F^3\) and \(U_{12}\). A.25 below constructs an actual involution with parity one in the image of \(\widehat{GT}_0\) at \(U_{12}\), and A.24 proves that this parity descends to that outer image. Thus the existence assertion at this specified relative level is proved. Lead 3 still needs a compatible order-two full lift. Neither R2 nor A.3 supplies that further equivariance. For a surjection \(G\to Q\) with kernel \(L\), a chosen lift \(t\) of an involution can be corrected to an involution \(ut\), \(u\in L\), exactly when \[ u(tut^{-1})=t^{-2}. \] Surjectivity asserts the existence of \(t\), not solvability of this nonabelian norm equation. The map \(C_4\to C_2\) disproves that implication in general, but is not a counterexample in the peripheral groups. The residual task is to solve the norm equations compatibly in the actual relative-level kernels with the specified frames and \(\Delta=1\), or to prove they are insoluble.
notes: A.25 gives an actual parity-one involution at U12; A.31 continues it compatibly through all relative principal-congruence levels. Complete dyadic/mixed-prime classification and arbitrary smaller characteristic levels remain open.

statement: Parity on arbitrary involutions For an involution \(\tau=(-1,f)\) in \(\widehat{GT}_0\), R3 gives \(\Delta(\tau)=\delta((1,f))\). It is zero for A.7's continuum family and for every \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-conjugate of \(c\). The cocycle relation alone gives only \(2\Delta(a)=0\) in \(\mathbb F_2\). A.25 gives such an involution in an actual relative outer image of \(\widehat{GT}_0\), but no full involution of parity one or universal full vanishing proof is obtained, in \(\widehat{GT}_0\) or \(\widehat{GT}\).
notes: A.25 and A.31 give Delta-one involutions in actual relative outer images and their congruence-tower inverse limit. No full Delta-one involution or universal full vanishing proof.

statement: The three full conjugacy assertions We have not decided whether every involution of \(\mathcal P,\widehat{GT}_0,\widehat{GT}\) is conjugate to \(c\) in its respective group. A.2 detects conjugacy of a fixed pair on all relative levels; A.11 identifies the equivalent peripheral generation condition. Neither supplies the compatible local conjugators or reflection triangles whose existence is required. For \S31, folios 198--199 verso, scans 391--394, the full finite-subgroup conclusion proved by R1 is that the only abstract possibilities in \(\mathcal P\) are \(1,C_2\), and \(C_2=\langle c\rangle\) occurs. Exhaustion of its embedding conjugacy classes is exactly the remaining assertion.
notes: All three full conjugacy assertions unresolved; no claim of complete resolution.

statement: The pronilpotent lifting kernel also has continuum many cohomology classes Put \(Q=\mathcal P_F\), \(\mathcal N=\ker(\mathcal P\to Q)\), and write \(c_Q\) for the image of \(c\). There is a canonical closed injection \[ C_Q(c_Q)/\langle c_Q\rangle \longrightarrow H^1(C_2,\mathcal N),\qquad \bar\beta\longmapsto[\beta c\beta^{-1}c]. \] Its image is exactly the \(\mathcal N\)-conjugacy classes in the fibre over \(c_Q\) which are conjugate to \(c\) in \(\mathcal P\). Both its domain and \(H^1(C_2,\mathcal N)\) have cardinality \(2^{\aleph_0}\). Thus the large cohomology set does not itself provide an additional full involution-conjugacy class.
notes: The large H1 is not evidence of an exotic full conjugacy class. All displayed classes are full P-conjugates of c.

statement: A prescribed reflection splits every pro-two extension of the symmetric group Let \(1\to K\to E\xrightarrow{q}S_3\to1\) be an extension of profinite groups with \(K\) pro-two. If a transposition \(t\in S_3\) has an involution lift \(\widetilde t\in E\), then there is a continuous section \(j:S_3\to E\) satisfying \(j(t)=\widetilde t\).
depends_on: Restriction/corestriction double-coset identities; finite extension cocycles; compactness
notes: The proof uses the special Sylow-2 double-coset structure of S3, not a general order-preserving lifting assertion.

statement: The parity-one relative frame can be chosen anti-invariant under conjugation In the notation of R2, put \(H_0=F'F^3\), \(\Gamma_2=\widehat B/O^2(H_0)\), and let \(d=\operatorname{Inn}(s)\circ c\), so that \(d(s)=s\), \(d(r)=r^{-1}\), \(d(x)=y^{-1}\), and \(d(y)=x^{-1}\). There is an actual element \[ b\in C_{H_0^{(2)}}(r),\qquad q(b)=[5I],\qquad d(b)=b^{-1}. \] Consequently the identity automorphism of \(\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(H_0)\), with \(s\)- and \(\tau\)-frames one and \(r\)-frame equal to \(b\) at two and one at all other primes, is a framed cocycle for conjugation by \(c\). Its modulo-twelve frame parity is one. This establishes local equivariance of these data; it does not assert an equivariant full lift.
depends_on: R2/E58 joint quotient; A.16; coprime complement conjugacy
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Task A.6; Lead 3
notes: Only local framed equivariance is proved. An R2 lift sigma has Delta=1 and (sigma c)^2 in the specified frame kernel L; the full norm equation in L remains open.

statement: R2 does not admit an unrestricted order-preserving refinement There is an actual involution of \(\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(F))\) which lifts to a full peripheral automorphism by R2 but has no involution lift in \(\mathcal P\).
depends_on: R1; R2; A.2; product decomposition in A.15
answers: Task A.2; Task A.4; Task A.5; Lead 3
notes: Refutes an unrestricted order-preserving strengthening of R2. The multiplier is mixed-sign; the globally negative fibre of A.17 remains open.

statement: The square obstruction at an abelian refinement and the character-lifting test Suppose \(a\) is a lift of a quotient involution, \(a^2\in L\), and \(L_0\triangleleft\langle L,a\rangle\) is contained in \(L\), with \(M=L/L_0\) finite abelian. Conjugation by \(a\) makes \(M\) a \(C_2\)-module. An involution exists above that quotient element in \(\langle L,a\rangle/L_0\) exactly when \[ [a^2]=0\quad\hbox{in}\quad H^2(C_2,M)=M^{a}/(1+a)M. \] This obstruction vanishes when \(M\) has odd order. For elementary abelian two-primary \(M\), its target is \(\ker(a+1)/\operatorname{im}(a+1)\). If \(\Delta\) has a continuous lift to a character \(\widehat{GT}_0\to\mathbb Z/4\), then it vanishes on every involution. The same conclusion follows from a continuous lift of \(\delta\) on \(\mathcal H\) which is invariant under conjugation by \(c\). Existence of either lift is not established here.
notes: Odd-primary abelian obstructions vanish; dyadic ones may survive. No global norm solution or Z/4 lift of Delta is proved.

statement: The locally glued symmetric subgroup does not lift in the standard extension Let \(H_0\), \(d\), and \(b\) be as in A.17. In the standard relative extension \[ \bigl(\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(H_0)\bigr) \rtimes\langle d\rangle \] there is a subgroup \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\simeq S_3\), generated by the named \(r\) and a transposition with component \(bd\) at two and \(d\) at every odd prime. No finite subgroup of the standard full extension \(\widehat B\rtimes\langle d\rangle\) maps onto \(S_{\mathrm{loc}}\). The obstruction is visible already in \(Q\rtimes\langle d\rangle\), with \(|Q|=576\).
depends_on: A.17; Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorems A-prime/B-prime/1; exact modulo12 sign calculation
notes: Blocks a lift inside the standard extension only. It is not an obstruction inside an unknown twisted extension associated with an exotic involution.

statement: Real projectivity and a rank-two open free subgroup do not imply finite graph recognition There exists a finitely generated real-projective profinite group \(E_*\) with an open normal subgroup isomorphic to \(\widehat F_2\), quotient \(C_2\), and self-centralizing involutions, which is not the profinite fundamental group of a finite graph of finite groups. It has one conjugacy class of involutions, so it does not satisfy R1's three-section conclusion.
depends_on: Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorems A-prime/B-prime/1 and open Kurosh; Pal-Quick2025 Theorem2.1
answers: A.7-A.8: full virtually free recognition route
notes: Explicit E*=C2 coproduct ((product odd Zp) semidirect Z2). It has one section class, so is not a counterexample to the three-section pants case.

statement: The three distinguished reflections normally generate, and a proper generated subgroup has infinite index Let \(\alpha\) and \(h\) be as in R1, and put \(E=F\rtimes_\alpha\langle t\rangle\), \(b=hyh^{-1}\). The three involutions \[ t_0=t,\qquad t_1=xt,\qquad t_2=b^{-1}t \] represent the three section classes and normally generate \(E\). If their closed generated subgroup \(J\) is proper, then \([E:J]\) is infinite. Normal generation alone does not supply the full generation required in A.11.
notes: Normal generation is strictly separated from the generation required by A.11; this does not prove existence of a generating reflection triangle.

statement: Torsion and cusp centralizers in the relative primary modular groups Let \(q:\widehat B=C_2\amalg C_3\to D\) be a finite quotient injective on the two factors, with torsion-free kernel \(U\), and write \[ \Gamma_p=\widehat B/O^p(U),\qquad V_p=U^{(p)}. \] For \(a=s\) or \(r\), of prime order \(\ell\), the following statements hold: \[ \begin{array}{ll} p\ne\ell:&C_{\Gamma_p}(a)\longrightarrow C_D(q(a)) \text{ is onto},\\[2pt] p=\ell:&C_{\Gamma_p}(a)=\langle a\rangle. \end{array} \] For \(U=U_{12}=\ker q_{12}\) in the projective modular quotient, put \(\Gamma=\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U)\). Then \[ C_{\Gamma_p}(\tau)=\overline{\langle\tau\rangle}, \qquad C_\Gamma(\tau)=\overline{\langle\tau\rangle} \simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] In the second formula the closure is taken in \(\Gamma\); in the first it is taken in \(\Gamma_p\).
depends_on: Open Kurosh; Herfort-Ribes1985 Theorem B-prime; Schur-Zassenhaus; boundary homology
notes: The coprime and equal-prime cases permit precise gluing of the literal r and s frames; the cusp statement includes x and y through sixth powers.

statement: The parity character descends to the actual outer image at level twelve Let \[ F_{12}=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_{12}),\qquad G_{12}=\operatorname{im}\!\left( \widehat{GT}_0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(F_{12})\right). \] The map is well-defined by the finite covariance in refereed LM7\_PUSH E.65, which preserves \(U_{12}\). There is a unique continuous character \(\Delta_{12}:G_{12}\to\mathbb F_2\) such that \(\Delta=\Delta_{12}\circ\pi_{12}\).
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Task A.6; Lead 3
notes: The proof identifies outer-trivial normalized multiplier-one actions with identity actions, so no accessory framed target is substituted for the required outer image.

statement: An actual parity-one involution exists at the relative level twelve The group \(G_{12}\) of A.24 contains an involution \(a_{12}\) with \[ \lambda(a_{12})=-1, \qquad\Delta_{12}(a_{12})=1. \] It is not conjugate to the image of \(c\) in \(G_{12}\). Thus the first, specified-relative-level assertion of Lead~3 holds at \(U_{12}\). The existence of an involution lifting it in the full group is not asserted.
depends_on: R2; R3 CM comparison; A.23; A.24
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Lead 3, first assertion
notes: Constructed by a cubed Galois c-cocycle at p=2 and identity at all other primes, with literal frames glued over Q12. A full lift remains a nonabelian norm equation in ker(GT0 to G12).

statement: Finite frame visibility prevents arithmetic-only continuation Put \[ U=U_{12},\qquad V=\overline{U'U^6},\qquad D_6=\widehat B/V. \] This is a finite quotient of order \(576\cdot6^{97}\), and \(V\) is characteristic in \(U\), normal in \(\widehat B\), and preserved by \(\widehat{GT}_0\). The two normalized CM bits of an element of \(\mathcal H\) are determined by its actual action on \(D_6\). In particular both bits are zero for an element acting identically on \(D_6\). Let \(H_6\) be the actual image of \(\mathcal H\) in \(\operatorname{Aut}(D_6)\), and \(J_6=\langle H_6,c_6\rangle\). There is a character \(\Delta_6:J_6\to\mathbb F_2\) induced by \(\Delta\) on \(\mathcal H\rtimes\langle c\rangle\). The involution of A.25 induces an actual involution \(a_6\in J_6\) with \(\Delta_6(a_6)=1\). No Galois element of multiplier \(-1\) has the same actual action on \(D_6\).
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Lead 3, continuation obstruction
notes: D6 has order 576*6^97. This excludes arithmetic-only componentwise continuation below its kernel; it does not exclude nongalois lifts or solve the full norm equation.

statement: The exact finite real-reflection count and its properness condition Let \(\pi:E\twoheadrightarrow D\) be an epimorphism of finite groups. Fix involutions \(d_0,d_1,d_2\in D\) which generate \(D\), and subsets \(T_{ij}\subseteq\pi^{-1}(d_id_j)\), for \((i,j)=(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\). For every subgroup \(J\leq E\), put \[ I_i(J)=\{u\in J:\pi(u)=d_i,\ u^2=1\}, \qquad M_{ij}(J)_{u,v}=\mathbf1_{T_{ij}}(uv). \] Thus \(M_{ij}(J)\) is a rectangular matrix with rows indexed by \(I_i(J)\) and columns indexed by \(I_j(J)\). The number of triples of involutions in \(E\) with the specified images and pair products, and which generate \(E\), is \[ \sum_{J\leq E}\mu(J,E) \operatorname{tr}\bigl(M_{01}(J)M_{12}(J)M_{20}(J)\bigr), \tag{A.27.1} \] where \(\mu\) is the ordinary subgroup-lattice M\"obius function. Empty index sets contribute zero. This count concerns actual homomorphisms from \(C_2*C_2*C_2\), with actual quotient data.
depends_on: Elementary matrix expansion and subgroup-lattice inversion
answers: Task A.5; Task A.7; Lead 3, equivariant R2 route
notes: A perfect-kernel S5/A5 control has 1000 weak reflection triples and no proper one. This general control is excluded by the actual pants conditions, as separately checked.

statement: A negative finite peripheral action is stopped by a central spin obstruction There is an epimorphism \(q:F\twoheadrightarrow A_6\) and an involutory automorphism \(\vartheta\) of \(A_6\) which sends each of the three labelled cusp images to an \(A_6\)-conjugate of its inverse, but no multiplier-minus-one peripheral automorphism of \(F\) satisfies \[ q\Phi=\vartheta q. \] In particular no full negative peripheral involution induces this finite action. The obstruction is already visible in a central double cover; it is not a counterexample to R2 or A.3.
depends_on: R1 for the separate section-incidence explanation; exact ATLAS-generator double-cover enumeration for the stronger central obstruction
answers: Task A.2; Task A.5; Task A.7; Lead 2; Lead 3, perfect-kernel controls
notes: The x,y,z passport is (4,4,4). All three cusp lifts require the nontrivial central character value, contradicting xyz=1. No R2 lift or characteristic-level automorphism is assumed.

statement: The new relative involution has exactly three section classes For the involution \(a_{12}\) constructed in A.25, choose its actual representative \(\phi c\) on \(F_{12}=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_{12})\). Then \[ \bigl|H^1(C_2,F_{12})\bigr|=3, \] where the action is this specified representative. Its relative dyadic component likewise has exactly three section classes and has trivial fixed subgroup in its orientation kernel. These are section classes of the group extension, not conjugacy classes of peripheral automorphisms.
depends_on: A.25; open Kurosh; Herfort-Ribes1985; odd-primary Schur-Zassenhaus
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Task A.7; Lead 3
notes: This computes H1(C2,F12) for the specified action, not H1(C2,H) or conjugacy of peripheral automorphisms. The new relative example already passes the three-section test.

statement: The level-twelve frames can also satisfy the involution relations The construction in A.25 can be made with its literal relative frames \(A,\beta\in\Gamma\) so that the associated r-normalizer and s-normalizer in \(\Gamma\rtimes\langle\phi c\rangle\) are actual subgroups \(S_3\) and \(C_2\times C_2\), with the finite frame values still \[ q(A)=1,\qquad q(\beta)=b. \] Consequently an R2 lift \(a=\widetilde\sigma c\) can be chosen with \[ a^2\in L_{12}^{\mathrm{fr}},\qquad L_{12}^{\mathrm{fr}} =\{k\in\mathcal H:\Phi_k|_\Gamma=1, \ A_k|_\Gamma=\beta_k|_\Gamma=1\}. \tag{A.30.1} \] This is a smaller kernel than the unframed \(L_{12}\). It does not assert a lift at a smaller characteristic level or solve the remaining norm equation.
notes: No smaller characteristic-level lift is claimed. The exact norm equation in the framed kernel is sufficient for the full lift; failure there alone would not exclude all unframed lifts.

statement: Parity-one involutions are compatible through the entire relative principal-congruence tower For every positive integer \(N\) divisible by twelve, put \[ \begin{gathered} Q_N=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/N)/\{\pm I\},\qquad U_N=\ker(\widehat B\longrightarrow Q_N),\\ \Gamma_N=\widehat B/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_N),\qquad F_N=F/R_{\mathrm{nil}}(U_N). \end{gathered} \] These kernels are preserved by the actual normalized \(\widehat{GT}_0\)-action. Let \(G_N\) be its actual outer image on \(F_N\). There is a single full element \(a\in\widehat{GT}_0\) such that \[ \lambda(a)=-1,\qquad \Delta(a)=1,\qquad a_N^2=1\quad\hbox{for every }12\mid N, \qquad a_N=\pi_N(a)\in G_N. \tag{A.31.1} \] The \(a_N\) are compatible and each has order exactly two. The character \(\Delta\) descends to every \(G_N\), and \(\Delta_N(a_N)=1\). In particular their inverse limit is an involution of parity one in the image of the full group on this entire tower. The assertion is restricted to this tower. The full element \(a\) is not proved to have order two, and the relative principal-congruence tower is not cofinal in the tower in A.2.
depends_on: A.23-A.25; R2; R3 global covariance and CM comparison; Marin2008 Section4 p776; inertia at three; compactness
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Lead 3, compatible congruence continuation
notes: The full a is not proved an involution. This relative tower is not cofinal: its common kernel maps onto A7. No claim about faithfulness of the GT0 action follows from that group-kernel fact.

statement: Congruence CM refinements cannot supply the invariant fourth-root character obstruction Let \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{cong}}\) be the image of \(\mathcal H\) on the family of actual groups \(\Gamma_N\), for \(12\mid N\). The character \(\delta=\Delta|_{\mathcal H}\) descends to this image. There is no continuous homomorphism \[ \eta:\mathcal H_{\mathrm{cong}}\longrightarrow \mathbb Z/4 \] whose reduction modulo two is \(\delta\) and which is invariant under conjugation by \(c\). The same exclusion applies to a proposed character on \(\mathcal H\) depending only on its congruence CM-frame data, including any refinement at moduli 24 or 48, or continuously on their entire tower.
answers: Task A.5; Task A.6; Lead 3, Bockstein route
notes: Covers CM refinements modulo 24 and 48 and the entire congruence frame tower. A global character using additional noncongruence data remains open.

statement: The compatible congruence family also has equivariant literal frames The full element \(a=hc\) in A.31 can be chosen so that its square belongs to \[ L_{\mathrm{cong}}^{\mathrm{fr}}= \bigcap_{12\mid N}\{k\in\mathcal H: \Phi_k|_{\Gamma_N}=1,\quad A_k|_{\Gamma_N}=\beta_k|_{\Gamma_N}=1\}. \tag{A.33.1} \] At every level, the literal r- and s-frames can therefore be retained with the actual finite normalizers \(S_3\) and \(C_2^2\) from A.30. This strengthens the compatible actual-action assertion without asserting a full order-two lift.
depends_on: A.16; A.23; A.30; A.31; elementary integral matrix conjugacy; R2; compactness
answers: Task A.4; Task A.5; Lead 3, compatible framed continuation
notes: The remaining norm equation is in L_cong-fr. No full order-two lift or arbitrary characteristic refinement is proved.

statement: The full peripheral lifting theorem holds over any closed normal relative kernel Let \(\Pi\) be either the full free three-cusp group \(F\), or the full modular group \(\widehat B\), with the respective three peripheral elements \((x,y,z)\) or \((s,r,\tau^{-1})\). Let \(V\triangleleft\Pi\) be any closed normal subgroup, without an openness or characteristicity assumption, and put \(R=R_{\mathrm{nil}}(V)\). Every continuous automorphism of \(\Pi/R\) preserving the three positive peripheral conjugacy classes, with specified literal conjugators there, lifts to a full peripheral automorphism of \(\Pi\) with those conjugators. The lift stabilizes \(R\). If a specified peripheral conjugator is one, that peripheral can be fixed literally. For infinitely many primes \(p\nmid2|Q|\), there are positive peripheral actions \(h_p\) on the actual finite quotient \[ N_p=\overline{[L,L]L^p},\qquad G_p=\Pi/N_p \tag{A.81.1} \] with all the following properties. Their negative companions \(b_p=h_pc_{G_p}\) are involutions fixing the literal negative cusp and admitting both norm-one normalizer frames above the prescribed Q-frames. The action extends to an involution on the \emph{actual first source-central refinement} \[ D_p=\Pi/\overline{[N_p,\Pi]}, \tag{A.81.2} \] again with literal cusp inversion and both norm-one frames. The corresponding positive action satisfies the ordinary lifting criterion: some full positive peripheral h induces \(h_p\), and h may fix \(\tau\) literally. Nevertheless, no full negative peripheral involution induces \(b_p\), even if its full cusp is only inverted up to conjugacy and no full normalizer frame is prescribed. Thus none of the ordinary full lifts of \(h_p\) can have involutory negative companion. This assertion concerns a constructed family at infinitely many eligible fresh primes; no particular such prime or enormous coefficient matrix is claimed to have been computed. Compatibility at every iterated central refinement is not asserted. The surviving \(W=0\) choices and the main existential problem remain open.

statement: The actual reflection augmentation module is projective at every prime and free at the dyadic prime Let \(E=F\rtimes C_2\), where \(F=\widehat F_2\), be one of the actual pants extensions already considered: the pure negative extension of C.28, or the regular extension of C.43. Let \(c_1,\ldots,c_n\) represent its involution classes, put \(C_i=\langle c_i\rangle\), and let \(\varepsilon\) be its orientation character. Here \(n=3\) in the first case and \(n=1\) in the second. For every prime p put \[ \Lambda_G=\mathbb Z_p[[G]],\qquad P_p=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z_p[[E/C_i]],\qquad R_p=\ker(P_p\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_p), \tag{A.82.1} \] where the last map sums the augmentations. These are actual compact modules over the full group E. For every finite discrete E-module A, the restriction maps satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} H^1(E,A)&\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^n H^1(C_i,A) &&\text{is onto},\\ H^2(E,A)&\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^n H^2(C_i,A) &&\text{is injective}. \end{aligned} \tag{A.82.2} \] Consequently \(R_p\) is finitely generated projective for every p, and \[ R_p\oplus(R_p\otimes\varepsilon)\simeq\Lambda_E^{\,n+1}, \qquad R_2\simeq\mathbb Z_2[[E]]^{(n+1)/2}. \tag{A.82.3} \] In particular the two dyadic ranks are two and one, respectively. This does not produce a finite graph of groups or a generating marked reflection system.
notes: Every finite coefficient is retained through projected centralizer heads and prescribed involution classes. Exact induction counit splits by projectivity, with compact finite-basis cancellation at two. Both incidence cokernels are explicit; target freeness does not prove selected generation or peripheral conjugacy.

statement: Actual odd finite-head twisted duality fixes all self-dual multiplicities Let E be the pure negative pants extension in A.82, and let K be an open normal subgroup of E contained in F. Put \(Q=E/K\), let \(k=\mathbb F_p\) for an odd prime p, and define the actual finite module \[ \overline R=k\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}(R_p)_K. \tag{A.83.1} \] In the Grothendieck group of finite \(k[Q]\)-modules, \[ [\overline R^*]=[\overline R\otimes\varepsilon]. \tag{A.83.2} \] If \(p\nmid|Q|\), this is an actual module isomorphism. Under this same prime-to-order hypothesis, A.82 and the isomorphism force every self-dual simple S to occur in \(\overline R\) with multiplicity \[ 2\dim_{\operatorname{End}_Q(S)}S. \tag{A.83.3} \] In particular, if every simple \(k[Q]\)-module is self-dual and \(p\nmid|Q|\), then \(\overline R\simeq k[Q]^2\). The nonself-dual paired blocks and the modular isomorphism problem are not removed by this statement.

For p not dividing head order this is an isomorphism and self-dual simples have twice their regular multiplicity. Nonselfdual ambiguity and marked generation remain Open.

statement: The actual compact augmentation module has orientation-twisted projective duality Let E be the pure negative pants extension of A.82. For every prime p put \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z_p[[E]]\) and let \(\iota:\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda\) be the continuous anti-involution induced by \(g\mapsto g^{-1}\). For a finitely generated projective compact left \(\Lambda\)-module P define its projective dual by \[ P^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda,\mathrm{cont}}(P,\Lambda), \qquad (a\cdot f)(v)=f(v)\iota(a). \tag{A.84.1} \] This is a compact left module; it is not the linear or Pontryagin dual of the underlying infinite compact abelian group. The actual module of A.82 satisfies \[ R_p^\#\simeq R_p\otimes\varepsilon. \tag{A.84.2} \] For every odd p and every finite head \(Q=E/K\), where \(K\trianglelefteq_o E\) and \(K\subseteq F\), the finite module \(\overline R=\mathbb F_p\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}(R_p)_K\) therefore satisfies the actual isomorphism \[ \overline R^*\simeq \overline R\otimes\varepsilon, \tag{A.84.3} \] including when \(p\mid |Q|\). More precisely, let S be a simple \(\mathbb F_p[Q]\)-module and \(P(S)\) its projective cover. If \(S\simeq S^*\), its projective cover occurs as a direct summand of \(\overline R\) exactly \[ 2\dim_{\operatorname{End}_Q(S)}S \tag{A.84.4} \] times. When every simple is self-dual, this gives \(\overline R\simeq\mathbb F_p[Q]^2\), without the prime-to-order restriction. In the modular case (A.84.4) concerns projective-cover summands, not composition-factor multiplicities. Neither (A.84.2) nor (A.84.4) removes the nonselfdual multiplicity ambiguity or proves the required incidence map surjective.

statement: The actual canonical Fox defect is induced under the joint Klein-four action Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\in\widehat{GT}_0\) be a nonidentity involution, and let \(u\in F'\) be its unique canonical parameter, where \(F=\widehat F(x,y)\). Thus \[ \alpha(x)=x^{-1},\quad \alpha(y)=f^{-1}y^{-1}f, \qquad u=f\alpha(u),\qquad \iota(u)=u^{-1}, \tag{A.85.1} \] and \(\iota\) interchanges x and y. Put \[ \begin{gathered} w=u^{-1}yu,\qquad \psi(x)=x,\quad\psi(y)=w, \qquad H=\overline{\langle x,w\rangle},\\ v=\operatorname{Inn}(u^{-1})\iota,\qquad \tau=\alpha v,\qquad V=\langle\alpha,v\rangle. \end{gathered} \tag{A.85.2} \] Then V is the actual Klein-four group acting on F and H. For every prime p use the full coefficient ring \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z_p[[F]]\), and define \[ \begin{gathered} B=1+(y-1)u_y,\qquad L_H=\Lambda(x-1)+\Lambda(w-1),\\ C_p=I_F/L_H \simeq\ker\bigl(\mathbb Z_p[[F/H]]\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_p\bigr). \end{gathered} \tag{A.85.3} \] The derivatives are the continuous left Fox derivatives specified below. The actual coset space \(X=F/H\) satisfies \[ X^\alpha=X^v=X^\tau=\{H\}. \tag{A.85.4} \] There is a closed pointed transversal \((Y,H)\) for its nontrivial V-orbits, and a compact \(\mathbb Z_p\)-module \(D_p=\ker(\mathbb Z_p[[Y]]\to\mathbb Z_p)\), such that \[ C_p\simeq\mathbb Z_p[V]\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}D_p \quad\hbox{as compact \(\mathbb Z_p[V]\)-modules}. \tag{A.85.5} \] In particular its Tate cohomology vanishes for V and every subgroup of V. The complete coupled full-ring Fox identities are (A.85.8)--(A.85.11) below. For any one p, \[ B\in\Lambda^\times \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C_p=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H=F. \tag{A.85.6} \] Neither (A.85.5) nor the coupled identities prove these equivalent conditions. The induced description is over the constant finite-group ring; no \(\Lambda\)-linear splitting or induced description is asserted.

statement: A canonical full cusp word compares the dihedral and relative Alexander units Retain the actual negative-\(\widehat{GT}_0\) data of A.85, and put \(z=(xy)^{-1}\), \(G_v=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle\). Let \(d=d_\alpha\) be the actual full unit from A.45: in the universal dihedral quotient \[ \pi(x)=a,\qquad\pi(y)=aT,\qquad\pi(u)=T^k, \qquad d=2k+1,\qquad k\in2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{A.86.1} \] In particular \(d_2\equiv1\pmod4\). There is a unique \(h_0\in F'\) satisfying \[ \tau(z)=h_0^{-1}z^{-1}h_0, \] and a unique \(q\in F\) such that \[ h_0\tau=q\tau q^{-1},\qquad q_{\mathrm{ab}}=(t,-t) \quad\text{for some }t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{A.86.2} \] Define actual full-group elements \[ \begin{gathered} e=(xu)v,\qquad b=q^{-1}eq,\qquad \Omega_\alpha=(x^dv)b^{-d}\in F,\\ \sigma=\operatorname{Inn}(h_0)\tau,\qquad g=e(qvq^{-1})=xu\,v(q)q^{-1}\in F. \end{gathered} \tag{A.86.3} \] Then \[ \begin{gathered} e^2=xy,\qquad\tau(b)=b^{-1},\qquad \sigma(g)g^{-1}=z,\\ a_{\mathrm{reg}}:=1-4t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\qquad (\Omega_\alpha)_{\mathrm{ab}} =\left(\frac{d-a_{\mathrm{reg}}}{2}, -\frac{d-a_{\mathrm{reg}}}{2}\right). \end{gathered} \tag{A.86.4} \] The element g is exactly C.44's unique solution for the normalized regular involution \(\sigma\); \(a_{\mathrm{reg}}\) is its image in \(F/\langle\!\langle z\rangle\!\rangle\), with generator the image of x. The full criterion is \[ \begin{aligned} \Omega_\alpha=1 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^du^{-1}y^du\sim_F(xy)^d\\ &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha\text{ is conjugate to }c\text{ in }\widehat{GT}_0. \end{aligned} \tag{A.86.5} \] If \(\alpha\in\widehat{GT}\), the last condition is also equivalent to conjugacy in \(\widehat{GT}\). These last group membership assertions use exactly A.39, with A.6 and A.36 for the respective descents, and A.45 for the fixed multiplier d. When (A.86.5) holds, the original cusp equation has the specified conjugator \[ x^du^{-1}y^du=q^{-1}(xy)^dq. \tag{A.86.6} \] It follows that the canonical Fox element of A.85 is a unit at every coefficient prime. No converse from that Fox-unit condition alone is asserted here. Neither \(a_{\mathrm{reg}}=d\) nor \(\Omega_\alpha=1\) is proved by this statement.

statement: The closure-intersection step is an unproved implication The proofs of Proposition 2.4 of \citet{Boggi2026} and Theorem 5.1(iii) of \citet{BoggiZalesskii2025} contain the same unproved passage. After the per-element comparisons, the equality that remains to be established is \[ \bigcap_{x\in S}\overline{C_G(x)} =\overline{\bigcap_{x\in S}C_G(x)} =\overline{C_G(H)},\qquad H=\langle S\rangle . \] Here \(S\) is a finite generating set of the finite subgroup \(H\leq G\), and all closures are in the specified profinite completion of \(G\). The cited per-element comparisons alone give only the inclusion from right to left. This observation does not refute either theorem. The exact published scopes must be retained. In Proposition 2.4, $G$ is assumed residually finite, good, and of finite virtual cohomological type; the assertion is quantified over every finite $H\leq G$. Its central conclusion is $Z_{\widehat G}(\iota(H))=\overline{\iota(Z_G(H))}$. In Theorem 5.1, a class $\mathscr C$ of finite groups is fixed. The group is residually $\mathscr C$, $\mathscr C$-good, and of finite virtual $p$-cohomological type at the relevant primes. Every finite solvable $\mathscr C$-subgroup has a normalizer with those same properties and with its full pro-$\mathscr C$ topology induced from $G$. Part (iii) asserts $C_{G_{\widehat{\mathscr C}}}(H)=\overline{C_G(H)}$ for every finite $\mathscr C$-subgroup $H$, while its normalizer assertion is restricted to solvable $H$. We audit these statements with their hypotheses, not a version in which goodness alone is substituted for all of them.

statement: The normalizer comparison repairs the solvable centralizer case Let \(G\) be residually finite and \(H\leq G\) finite. If \(N_{\widehat G}(H)=\overline{N_G(H)}\), then \[ C_{\widehat G}(H)=\overline{C_G(H)}. \] In particular the centralizer conclusion of Boggi--Zalesskii, Theorem 5.1, is justified for solvable \(H\) under that theorem's two hypotheses, by its independently proved normalizer assertion.

statement: The exact coset obstruction Let \(U\trianglelefteq G\) have finite index and \(U\cap H=1\). Write \(\widehat U=\overline U\leq\widehat G\). For \(\bar g\in C_{G/U}(\bar H)\), choose \(g\in G\) mapping to \(\bar g\) and put \[ a_g(h)=ghg^{-1}h^{-1}\in U\qquad(h\in H). \] With \(H\) acting on \(U\) by conjugation, this is a nonabelian one-cocycle. The class \([a_g]\in H^1(H,U)\) is independent of the choice of \(g\) in the left coset \(Ug\). Then \[ \begin{split} \bar g\in\im\bigl(C_G(H)\to G/U\bigr) &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ [a_g]=1\text{ in }H^1(H,U),\\ \bar g\in\im\bigl(C_{\widehat G}(H)\to G/U\bigr) &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ [a_g]=1\text{ in }H^1(H,\widehat U). \end{split} \] Hence centralizer equality is equivalent to triviality of the completion kernel on these \emph{coset obstruction classes}, at every \(U\).

statement: The level-five kernel is characteristic Every continuous epimorphism \(\widehat B=\widehat{C_2*C_3}\twoheadrightarrow A_5\) has the same kernel \(\widehat K\). In particular \(\widehat K\) is characteristic in \(\widehat B\).

statement: A centerless extension comparison Let \(1\to L\to E\to H\to1\) be an exact sequence of profinite groups, with \(L\) centerless, \(C_E(L)=1\), \(H\) centerless, and \(L\) characteristic in \(E\). View \(H\) as a subgroup of \(\Out(L)\) through conjugation. Then restriction induces a canonical isomorphism \[ \ker\bigl(\Out(E)\longrightarrow\Out(H)\bigr) \ \simeq\ C_{\Out(L)}(H). \] The groups carry their profinite automorphism topologies when they are topologically finitely generated.

statement: The peripheral icosahedral comparison Let \(\Out_{\partial}(\widehat K)\) denote continuous outer automorphisms permuting the twelve conjugacy classes of cusp inertia, with a common unit multiplier. statement: Purity and the discrete centralizer The multiplier-one subgroup in B.6 acts trivially on the twelve puncture labels. statement: Explicit periodic braids over the icosahedral action Put \(Z=\Delta_{12}^{2}\), where \(\Delta_{12}=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{11})(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{10}) \cdots(\sigma_1\sigma_2)\sigma_1\) is the Garside half twist in the discrete Artin braid group \(B_{12}\). There are explicit braids \(\beta_2=\Delta_{12}\) and \(\beta_3\) satisfying \[ \beta_2^2=\beta_3^3=Z. \] We specify \(\beta_3\) by listing the indices of its positive letters, in multiplication order: \[ \begin{gathered} 1,11,5,7,10,2,9,3,8,4,2;\\ 7,3,6,2,5,4,3,2,7,10,6;\\ 1,7,9,10,8,5,9,7,2,6,10;\\ 5,4,7,3,5,8,4,2,5,7,6. \end{gathered} \] With \(a=\beta_2\beta_3^{-1}\) and \[ R_{12}=\sigma_{11}\sigma_{10}\cdots\sigma_2\sigma_1^2 \sigma_2\cdots\sigma_{10}\sigma_{11}, \] the stronger Artin-group identity is \[ a^5=Z R_{12}^{-1}. \] Consequently the images in \(B_{12}(S^2)\), where \(R_{12}=1\), satisfy \(a^5=\beta_3^3=(a\beta_3)^2=Z\) and generate the binary icosahedral group of order \(120\). Their mapping-class image is the icosahedral \(A_5\).

statement: The normalizer formulation and its three-coset test Let \(E=\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12],1}\), with the usual completed Birman homomorphism \(p:E\to\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]}\), and identify \(\widehat B=p^{-1}(A_5)\). Restriction of conjugation gives \[ N_E(\widehat B)\longrightarrow\Out(\widehat B). \] Its image is exactly \(\mathcal K\). For a multiplier-one representative normalized by \(\Phi(\tau)=\tau\), with frames \(\Phi(s)=\beta_\Phi s\beta_\Phi^{-1}\) and \(\Phi(r)=A_\Phi r A_\Phi^{-1}\), membership in \(\mathcal K\) is equivalent to \[ C_E(\tau)\cap\beta_\Phi C_E(s)\cap A_\Phi C_E(r)\ne\varnothing. \]

statement: The properly typed tripod tests For \(\Phi\in\mathcal H\) and a fixed three-subset \(t\) of the twelve labelled cusps, let \(N_t\trianglelefteq\widehat K\) be the closed normal subgroup generated by all other cusp subgroups. Then restriction and quotient define a continuous homomorphism \[ \mathfrak T_t:\mathcal H\longrightarrow \Out_{\partial}(\widehat K/N_t)\cong\mathcal P. \] The last identification requires an ordered identification of the three surviving cusps with \(0,1,\infty\). We have \(\mathfrak T_t(\mathcal K)=1\) and \(\mathcal K\cap G_{\mathbb Q}=1\), for the specified faithful Galois embedding. The same test is defined on any subgroup fixing the three-subset setwise; it is not automatically a map for every element of the larger group in B.6 and every labelled three-subset.

statement: The topological quintic resolvent and its distinct quotient types The preimage \(\Gamma_T\leq B\) of an \(A_4\leq A_5\) has signature \((0;2,3,3;\infty)\) and presentation \(C_2*C_3*C_3\). Its degree-five modular map has the model \[ j=t^3(t^2+5t+40),\qquad j-1728=(t-3)(t^2+4t+24)^2. \] The two unramified points above \(j=0\), hence the two order-three orbifold points, are conjugate over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-15})\). Filling either order-three point gives \(C_2*C_3\); filling the order-two point gives \(C_3*C_3\), not \(C_2*C_3\).

statement: The proposed identities on the full Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group B.53 below proves P4's exact quadratic-character domain, both quintic homomorphisms, their arithmetic identity, and the kernel inclusion for $\mathcal K$. Its third map has the corrected weighted-orbifold target $\operatorname{Out}_{\partial}(C_3\amalg C_3)$. B.55 constructs a nonempty set of full R2 lifts $\Phi\in\mathcal H$ for which $\mathfrak T_\pm(\Phi)\ne\Phi$, proving the first assertion of P5. B.57 refutes P7's full common-kernel equality by a separate full central-extension construction. What remains undecided here is the assertion that $\mathfrak T_\pm$ fixes every element of $\widehat{GT}\cap D$. That assertion does not follow from the arithmetic restriction or from a linearized calculation. The exact source distinction is decisive: Nakamura--Schneps, Theorem 1.1 and Definition 1.1, prove their additional relations on the Galois image and use them to define the subgroup \(I\Gamma\); Theorem 1.2 proves that it is a subgroup containing that image \citep{NakamuraSchneps2000}. These statements do not assert that all of \(\GT\) satisfies the new relations. Hoshi--Mochizuki--Tsujimura, Definition 3.3, retain the additional COF and RGC conditions in their BGT framework \citep{HoshiMochizukiTsujimura2025}. Replacing those groups by \(\GT\) would remove a hypothesis. The unresolved requirement is a proof of that replacement, or a concrete element violating the claimed identity, together with its typed restriction maps.

statement: An exact list of the 495 cross-ratio pairs Let \(T\leq\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb Q(i))\) be generated by \[ u\longmapsto-u,\qquad u\longmapsto1/u,\qquad u\longmapsto\frac{u+i}{u-i}. \] It is tetrahedral of order twelve. Label its twelve elements in the order of the breadth-first construction in \texttt{code/crossratio\_495.py}, and write \(g_j(u)=(a_ju+b_j)/(c_ju+d_j)\). The ordered tetrahedral parameter curve is \[ S_T=\mathbb P^1\setminus E,\qquad E=\{\infty\}\cup V\bigl(u(u^4-1)(u^8+14u^4+1)\bigr); \] it has fourteen punctures and fundamental group \(F_{13}\). There is an explicit labelling of \[ S_5=\mathbb P^1\setminus\bigl(\{0,\infty\}\cup\mu_5\bigr), \qquad (0,\infty,1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^4, t,t\omega,\ldots,t\omega^4) \] which agrees at an icosahedral basepoint with the tetrahedral labelling. For each increasing four-subset \(q=(i,j,k,l)\), the attached \texttt{data/crossratio\_495.csv} gives the rational functions \(\psi_q:S_T\to M_{0,4}\) and \(\phi_q:S_5\to M_{0,4}\), with that common basepoint. We use the ordered covers: on the unlabelled quotient tripods a fixed four-subset need not be invariant under the label monodromy.

statement: The paired four-point equations have nontrivial discrete solutions There is an explicit nonidentity word \(w\in\pi_1(S_T,u_0)\) such that \[ \psi_{q*}(w)=1=\phi_{q*}(1) \qquad\text{for all }q\in\binom{\{1,\ldots,12\}}4. \] The same equalities hold after full profinite completion. Thus these equations alone do not characterize the icosahedral centralizer: they already admit noncentralizing discrete tetrahedral braids.

statement: The degree-one coprime fixed group and the direction of its lifting Let \(P=\Gamma_{0,12}\) be the pure discrete group, and let \(P^{(\ell)}\) be its pro-\(\ell\) completion. Conjugation by the specified geometric \(A_5\) defines a genuine action on it. For \(\ell\nmid60\), \[ C_{P^{(\ell)}}(A_5)\longrightarrow (P^{(\ell),\mathrm{ab}})^{A_5}\cong\mathbb Z_\ell^2 \] is onto. Thus the fixed group is infinite. Under the continuous geometric outer action on \(\widehat K^{(\ell)}\), every such fixed element has the same relative pro-\(\ell\) outer action as some element of \(\mathcal H\), obtained by R2 for \(U=K\). This asserts lifting to \(\mathcal H\), not lifting to \(C_{\widehat\Gamma}(A_5)=\mathcal K\).

statement: The sixfold cyclic cover and its multiplicity-free representation Let \(X\) be the smooth compactification of the cyclic cover of the twelve-punctured icosahedral sphere which sends every positive cusp meridian to \(1\in C_6\). Its genus is \(25\). With \(E=\mathbb Q(\zeta_6)=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\), its primitive-character cohomology has dimension ten over \(E\). The \(A_5\)-representation on it is \[ V=V_1\oplus V_4\oplus V_5, \qquad\dim_E V_i=i, \] where all three constituents are absolutely irreducible and occur once. Its polarization has signature \((1,9)\), with the one-dimensional constituent of one sign and the other two of the opposite sign. The unramified cover is the fibre product defined by \(K\cap B'\leq B\). This is a congruence subgroup of exact level thirty, and \(B/(K\cap B')\cong A_5\times C_6\).

statement: Three ordinary linear characters do not exist on the stated full domain Lead 7's construction does not give three ordinary unit-valued characters on every element of \(\{\Phi\in\GTzero:\lambda\equiv\pm1\pmod5\}\). Complex conjugation, which belongs to that domain, exchanges the two primitive sixth-root eigenspaces. On a single \(E\)-module its action is semilinear. The valid scalar constructions must first restrict to \(\lambda\equiv1\pmod6\), or have a semilinear target and a crossed multiplication law.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The real compact torus and its congruence centralizer Write \(\mathcal O_E=\mathbb Z[\zeta_6]\) and let \(\Lambda\) be the rank-ten Eisenstein lattice of the twelve-equal-weight Deligne--Mostow representation. Its projective arithmetic group is the projectivization of \(\Aut(\Lambda)\), with Hermitian signature \((1,9)\). The algebraic centralizer of the icosahedral image in the projective unitary group is the \(\mathbb Q\)-torus \[ T=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}^{,1}_{E/\mathbb Q}\mathbb G_m\bigr)^3 /\operatorname{Res}^{,1}_{E/\mathbb Q}\mathbb G_m, \] the denominator embedded diagonally. It has dimension two and is compact over \(\mathbb R\). For \(\ell\nmid30\), put \(U_\ell^1=\{u\in(\mathcal O_E\otimes\mathbb Z_\ell)^\times: u\bar u=1\}\). The centralizer in the local congruence closure is the projective image of \[ \left\{(u_1,u_4,u_5)\in(U_\ell^1)^3: u_1u_4^4u_5^5\in\mu_3\right\}. \tag{B.23.1} \] In particular it is infinite. This is a computation in the congruence quotient of the lattice, not in \(\widehat\Gamma\).
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The exact lifting obstruction and the four-point control Let \(\rho:\widehat\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L\) be any specified compact quotient, put \(N=\ker\rho\), and suppose \(A_5\) embeds in \(L\). For \(t\in C_L(A_5)\), choose \(g\in\widehat\Gamma\) lifting it and define \[ a_t(h)=ghg^{-1}h^{-1}\in N\qquad(h\in A_5). \] Then \([a_t]\in H^1(A_5,N)\) is independent of the chosen lift, and \(t\) lifts to \(\mathcal K\) if and only if \([a_t]=1\). This applies to every element of (B.23.1). At four points the analogous discrepancy can be computed fully: in the modular quotient \(\widehat{C_2*C_3}\), the centralizer of the geometric \(C_3\) is just \(C_3\), whereas its congruence centralizer contains a one-dimensional norm-one torus. Precisely the three elements of \(C_3\) have trivial lifting obstruction in that quotient.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: Solvable triangular controls and levels three and four For a finite solvable geometric group \(G\leq\Gamma_{0,[n]}\), the independently proved normalizer comparison, together with B.2, gives the centralizer comparison. If its punctured quotient is a triangle orbifold, the discrete normalizer modulo deck transformations is finite. The pure part of its completed centralizer is therefore trivial. In particular the tetrahedral and octahedral groups give \(\mathcal K_3=\mathcal K_4=1\). At six equal-weight points the octahedral representation has a two-summand scalar commutant and an infinite compact local torus, although only the identity can lift from that torus to the full geometric centralizer.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The arithmetic local calculation does not decide the global centralizer For twelve points we have not determined which elements of (B.23.1) have trivial class in \(H^1(A_5,\ker(\widehat\Gamma\to L_\ell))\). Neither compactness at the real place nor strong approximation computes this nonabelian cohomology set. Thus Lead 6's infinite congruence centralizer is verified, but it proves neither \(\mathcal K=1\) nor its negation. The formulas at \(\ell\mid30\) need integral representations with their nonsplit isotypic lattices; the good-prime decomposition has not been extended to those primes in this return.

statement: The remaining arithmetic-character calculations The normalized Jacobi-sum values on \(G_{\mathbb Q(\zeta_{15})}\), the values for the R2 lifts at \(U=K\) and level thirty, and vanishing on \(\mathcal K\) remain undecided. B.21 supplies the cover and the precise rational representation; B.22 corrects the domains, the deck ambiguity, and the integral projector issue before any such calculation is meaningful. Since no vanishing has been proved, the proposed implication to the two Fibonacci representations has not been used.

statement: The pure tetrahedral and cyclic intersection Put $P=P\Gamma_{0,12}$, choose the named $T=A_4$ and $D=C_5$ inside the geometric $A_5$, and put \[ H_T=C_P(T),\qquad H_5=C_P(D). \] In the full profinite completion of the pure mapping class group, \[ \mathcal K=C_{\widehat P}(A_5) =\widehat{H_T}\cap\widehat{H_5},\qquad H_T\simeq F_{13},\quad H_5\simeq F_6, \qquad H_T\cap H_5=1. \] Both displayed completions are their actual embedded closures in $\widehat P$. The ordered parameter curves and their basepoint choices are those of B.18. In particular the equality is an intersection in one specified ambient group, not an abstract intersection of two unrelated free profinite groups.
notes: The complete scoped statement is included in this field; LaTeX formulas retain the paper notation.

statement: The precise arithmetic normalizer restriction Let $X/k$ be a smooth affine hyperbolic curve over a number field, with geometric fundamental group $F=\pi_1(X_{\overline k})$ and arithmetic fundamental group $E=\pi_1(X)$. Let $1\ne A\leq F$ be closed and procyclic, and suppose that a closed subgroup $N\leq E$ normalizes $A$ and has image $G_L\leq G_k$, with $L/k$ finite. For a finite Galois extension $M/\mathbb Q$ containing $L$, let $\mathcal P_M$ be the rational primes unramified in $M$ whose Frobenius class is the class of a complex conjugation in $\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb Q)$. Then either $A$ is contained in a unique cusp inertia group, or \[ A_\ell=1\quad(\ell\in\mathcal P_M). \tag{B.29.1} \] Consequently cofinite prime support implies cuspidality. If $L$ is totally real, every such $A$ is cuspidal, without a prime-support condition. These are cuspidality conclusions, not nonexistence conclusions in an arbitrary curve group.
depends_on: Stix Theorem20 and Proposition11/Corollaries12–13; Serre local algebraicity; explicit descent
notes: Repairs missing N←AN step; corrects LM6A14 citation; cuspidality rather than nonexistence; all primes if normalizer field totally real.

statement: The tetrahedral centralizer has its full profinite topology Let $T=A_4$ act on the twelve vertices and put $F_T=C_{\Gamma_{0,[12]}}(T)$. The natural map \[ \widehat{F_T}\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]} \tag{B.30.1} \] is injective, and its image is exactly $C_{\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]}}(T)$. In particular $F_T\simeq F_2$ gives $\overline{F_T}\simeq\widehat F_2$, and the pure subgroup $F_T\cap\Gamma_{0,12}\simeq F_{13}$ also has its full profinite topology induced from the ambient mapping class group.
depends_on: Boggi2026 §§3.1–3.2 restricted to p-groups; BZ2025TheoremA; V4/C3 induction; finite-extension topology

statement: A totally real arithmetic model at the icosahedral point For the tetrahedral action generated by \[ u\longmapsto-u,\qquad u\longmapsto1/u, \qquad u\longmapsto\frac{u+i}{u-i}, \] the curve of unlabelled free orbits is the $\mathbb Q$-curve \[ C_T=\mathbb P^1_v\setminus\{\infty,6\sqrt{-3},-6\sqrt{-3}\}, \qquad v=\frac{u^{12}-33u^8-33u^4+1}{u^2(u^4-1)^2}. \tag{B.31.1} \] In the embedding used for the cross-ratio computation, the icosahedral point is $v_0=-22\sqrt5/5\in C_T(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5))$. The injection \[ \pi_1(C_{T,\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overline v_0) \simeq\widehat F_2\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_{0,[12]} \tag{B.31.2} \] has image $\overline{F_T}$. For the actual Galois action defined by the rational point $v_0$ and its image family, $\mathcal K\leq\overline{F_T}$ is stable under the full group $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$.
notes: Unlabelled curve overQ, v0=−22√5/5; actual full G_Q√5 normalization via rational-point section and family, not unspecified open subgroup.

statement: No tetrahedral cusp inertia meets the icosahedral kernel For every cusp inertia group $I$ of $\pi_1(C_{T,\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overline v_0)$, including every conjugate inertia group, \[ I\cap\mathcal K=1. \tag{B.32.1} \] The statement concerns the whole $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ inertia, including subgroups supported at one prime.

statement: The abelian case of Lead 8 and the cofinite-support exclusion For the actual subgroup $\mathcal K$ of the question, \[ \mathcal K\text{ abelian} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal K=1. \tag{B.33.1} \] Moreover $\mathcal K$ has no nontrivial closed procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer on $C_T$ and nonzero pro-$p$ component at all but finitely many rational primes. The same exclusion holds with arbitrary prime support if the normalizer projects onto the Galois group of a totally real number field.

notes: Actual K abelian⇒K=1. Cofinite-support procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer cannot lie inK. Does not prove K abelian.

statement: The missing commutativity assertion in Lead 8 It remains undecided here whether $\mathcal K$ is abelian. No two noncommuting elements of $\mathcal K$ have been constructed either. B.33 proves that this is equivalent, for this particular group, to the unresolved assertion $\mathcal K=1$. The arithmetic restriction supplies no way to extract from an arbitrary nonabelian $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$-stable closed subgroup of $\widehat F_2$ a nontrivial procyclic subgroup with open arithmetic normalizer. A chosen element's procyclic closure need not have an open stabilizer. Similarly, projecting $\mathcal K$ to a pro-$p$ or metabelian quotient does not establish commutativity in the full group. These are the exact remaining steps in the two arithmetic approaches attempted here. The finite cross-ratio and rigid-subconfiguration tests in the other subsections impose necessary constraints but do not repair this inference.
depends_on: B.33; necessary finite and rigid-subconfiguration tests
notes: Neither commutativity nor two noncommuting full elements established; arithmetic stability does not give open normalizer of a chosen cyclic closure.

statement: A sufficient product-separability condition with its quantifiers Let $G$ be residually finite and $H,J\leq G$. Suppose that for every finite-index normal subgroup $U\trianglelefteq G$ the product $(H\cap U)(J\cap U)$ is closed in the profinite topology of $G$. Then \[ \overline H\cap\overline J=\overline{H\cap J} \quad\hbox{inside }\widehat G. \] Applied to $H_T,H_5$ in B.28, this condition would prove $\mathcal K=1$. B.52 proves the unrefined product $H_TH_5$ is closed. The refined condition above remains unresolved; B.46--B.49 and B.52 explain exactly why the unrefined result does not yet establish it.

statement: The audited centralizer dependencies do not use the nonsolvable equality The finite-subgroup comparisons used in LM6 C.16--C.17 are involution comparisons. The torsion-centralizer comparisons in LM7\_PUSH E.64 are cyclic-factor comparisons; its sewing comparison uses the specified twist stabilizer and genus-two congruence identification. ANABELIAN\_149\_PUSH A.29l uses the separate orbifold theorem of Boggi--Zalesskii (2019), Lemma 3.1. None of these passages uses the unproved nonsolvable closure-intersection equality in B.1.

statement: The level-six control also has trivial residual kernel For $N=2,3,4,6$, the group $\mathcal K_N$ of task B.5 is trivial. For $N=6$ this uses the full profinite mapping class group of the genus-one curve $Y(6)$ with its twelve cusps; it is not a prime-by-prime linear computation.

statement: The remaining congruence levels No determination of $\mathcal K_N$ for all $N$ is obtained here. In particular $\mathcal K_5=1$ is the main unresolved assertion, and the corresponding level-seven and level-eleven kernels remain undecided. Their quotient compactifications have genera three and twenty-six, respectively. An index-seven or index-eleven resolvent alone supplies neither an injective comparison back to the original group nor a simultaneous lifting theorem inside the profinite mapping class group. For levels with higher genus one must additionally distinguish the image in the loop-outer group from the abstract full mapping class completion and its congruence kernel. Even when $N\mid M$, this paper does not assert $\mathcal K_M\subseteq\mathcal K_N$ without proving the required equivariant profinite covering-descent comparison.

statement: The nonsolvable direction and the published assertions For a finite solvable subgroup of a genus-zero mapping class group, the centralizer is the closure of the discrete centralizer, by the prime-power normalizer induction in B.30 and the open-kernel argument B.2. This proves the solvable direction of the refined triangle-orbifold statement in task B.6. For $A_5$ on twelve vertices the reverse direction would assert $\mathcal K\ne1$, which remains undecided. Accordingly Conjecture $2^-$ is not proved or refuted here. Neither Boggi's Proposition 2.4 and Theorem C(iii), nor Boggi--Zalesskii's Theorem 5.1(iii), is refuted by this audit. Their nonsolvable centralizer conclusions remain unsupported by the displayed proofs at the step B.1 isolates. Boggi's Theorem A in its general ramified nonsolvable case also retains the missing input in Lemma 3.2, where the configuration-group centralizer is identified using Proposition 2.4. The free-action proof in Section 3.1 and the prime-power repairs above do not use that missing step. For a particular action whose discrete centralizer is already trivial, its own congruence property is tautological; that observation does not prove the general ramified theorem or the ambient profinite centralizer comparison.

statement: The complete relative images and the bad-prime refinements remain undetermined B.20 proves the stated coprime pro-$\ell$ invariant construction and a lift to the full peripheral group. It does not determine the full relative images requested at $U=K$ or at $U=K'K^p$ for $p=2,3,5$. Membership in the actual profinite mapping class image is equivalently the normalizer or three-coset equation in B.9. B.54 now constructs relative data at $U=K$, at the good prime seven, for which every full peripheral R2 lift has a nontrivial tripod action. None is a braid lift. Thus the universal assertion that R2 can always be carried out inside that braid image is false. This obstruction does not classify the two complete relative images or their intersection, nor their compatibility over finer characteristic levels. No computation in this paper suppresses the primes $2,3,5$ or upgrades coprime invariant lifting to those primes.

statement: Parity and further-orbit lifting in the hypothetical nontrivial kernel If $\mathcal K\ne1$, neither the restriction of $\Delta$ to all its elements nor its extension along every required icosahedral marked-orbit locus has been determined. The latter extension would have to be constructed with compatible based maps and then checked against the pentagon; it does not follow from centralization of $A_5$ at one level. B.10 does prove that a nonidentity element of $\mathcal K$ which also satisfied the pentagon would lie outside the Galois image. No such element or complete lifting chain is constructed here. This conditional implication is retained without using it as evidence that either hypothesis holds.

statement: A nontrivial arithmetic ambiguity in every E.58 lift Put $H_0=F'F^3\trianglelefteq\widehat B$ and \[ R_{\rm sol}=\bigcap_{G_{\mathbb Q}\twoheadrightarrow D, \ D\ \mathrm{finite\ solvable}}\ker(G_{\mathbb Q}\to D). \] This is a nontrivial closed subgroup of $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For every $\sigma\in R_{\rm sol}$, the normalized modular automorphism induced by $\sigma$ has multiplier one and is the identity on $\widehat B/R_{\rm nil}(H_0)$. Its two canonical pure accessory frames have image one in this same relative quotient. Consequently right multiplication by any such $\sigma$ preserves every prescribed relative automorphism and relative frame coordinate in the construction of LM7\_PUSH E.58, including its finite modulo-twelve frame classes.

statement: A finite simple group excluded uniformly from these relative levels Let $S=A_{10000}$. No subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_d(\mathbb F_p)$, for $d\leq97$ and any prime $p$, has $S$ as a quotient of a subgroup. Consequently every finite section of a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_d^{(p)})$ also avoids $S$.

statement: A simultaneous nontrivial arithmetic kernel for both lifting data Let $N_{12}=\ker(\widehat B\to \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/12)/\{\pm I\})$. There is a nontrivial closed subgroup $Z\leq G_{\mathbb Q}$ with multiplier one whose normalized automorphisms and both canonical accessory frames are the identity at every relative pro-$p$ level over $H_0$ and over $N_{12}$, simultaneously. Thus it kills the whole relative pronilpotent source and the specified relative frame coordinates in both LM7\_PUSH E.58 and LM7 D.46.

statement: The relative prescriptions leave all tripod and corrected resolvent values undetermined Fix any actual full lift $\Phi$ allowed by LM7\_PUSH E.58, or by R2 applied to the specified relative action and frames of LM7 D.46. For the subgroup $Z$ of B.44, every $\Phi\sigma$, $\sigma\in Z$, is another allowed lift with the same relative data. For every three-subset $t$ of the icosahedral cusps, the map \[ Z\longrightarrow\mathcal P, \qquad \sigma\longmapsto \mathfrak T_t(\Phi\sigma) \tag{B.45.1} \] is injective. The same is true of $\sigma\mapsto\mathfrak R(\Phi\sigma)$ for each of the three typed resolvent homomorphisms $\mathfrak R$ constructed in B.53: the first two have target $\widehat{GT}_0$, and the third has the peripheral outer automorphism group of $C_3\amalg C_3$ as its target. Thus neither existential construction specifies a single value of any tripod test or of any of these corrected resolvent maps. At most one element of the coset $\Phi Z$ can belong to $\mathcal K$.

statement: The exact refined-product criterion For subgroups $H,J$ of a residually finite group $G$, the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $HJ$ is closed in the profinite topology of $G$, and $\overline H\cap\overline J=\overline{H\cap J}$ in $\widehat G$; \item for every finite-index subgroup $L\leq G$ containing $H\cap J$, the subset $(H\cap L)J$ is closed in that topology. \end{enumerate} This is \citet[Theorem 1.1]{DE_Minasyan2023}; its proof is Proposition 2.4 together with Proposition 3.1. For the actual $P,H_T,H_5$ of B.28, it gives the equivalence \[ \left\{\begin{array}{c} H_TH_5\text{ is closed in }P,\\ \mathcal K=1 \end{array}\right. \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (H_T\cap L)H_5\text{ is closed in }P \quad\text{for every }L\leq_f P. \] Equivalently, every product $H_0J_0$ is closed for finite-index $H_0\leq H_T$ and $J_0\leq H_5$. The quantifier over refinements cannot in general be omitted.
answers: Part B.4(c) exact missing product condition
notes: Includes independent proof for trivial discrete intersection; one unrefined product is not enough.

statement: A closed product with a nontrivial profinite intersection Let $V=M_2(\mathbb Z)$ additively, let $S=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ act on $V$ by left multiplication, and put \[ G=V\rtimes S, \qquad H=\{(0,B):B\in S\}, \qquad J=(I,1)H(I,1)^{-1}. \] Then $G$ is residually finite, $H\cap J=1$, and $HJ$ is closed in the full profinite topology of $G$. Both factors have the full induced profinite topology; every finite-index subgroup of either factor is separable in $G$. Nevertheless \[ \overline H\cap\overline J \cong\ker\bigl(\widehat{\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)} \longrightarrow\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z})\bigr) \ne1. \] In fact this intersection has a quotient isomorphic to $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_8)$. This is the example of \citet[Example 4.1]{DE_Minasyan2023}, with the failure witnessed here by an explicit finite quotient. It is a counterexample to the general implication from one closed product to equality of intersections. It is not a counterexample to the icosahedral assertion.
answers: Part B.4(c) correction of the general product-closure implication
notes: Full semidirect-product topology proved; all finite-index factor subgroups individually separable; not a counterexample for the actual icosahedral centralizer. The failure also persists in the torsion-free ambient subgroup M2(Z) semidirect Gamma(3), with both factors free of rank three.

statement: The hypotheses of the recent separability criteria Put $\Pi=\pi_1(S^2\setminus V_{12})\cong F_{11}$ and use the faithful Dehn--Nielsen map $P\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$. For $H\leq P$, write \[ \widetilde H=\{\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Pi): [\alpha]\in H\}. \] If $\widetilde H$ is conjugacy separable, then $H$ is separable in $\operatorname{Out}(\Pi)$, and therefore in $P$. This is the exact specialization of \cite[Corollary D]{DE_FournierFacio2025}. For $H=H_T,H_5$ the preimages are, after choosing lifts of free bases, $F_{11}\rtimes F_{13}$ and $F_{11}\rtimes F_6$. The cited criterion concerns individual subgroups and does not assert closure of their products.
notes: Multitwists rule out convex cocompactness; no suitable relative-hyperbolic or central-extension ambient comparison proved for products.

statement: A finite-action reformulation of every refined product Retain the fixed embedding $\iota:A_5\hookrightarrow \Gamma=\Gamma_{0,[12]}$, with the generating subgroups $T=A_4$ and $D=C_5$, and identify them with their images. Let $L\leq_f P$ and $g\in P$. Then $g$ belongs to the closure of $(H_T\cap L)H_5$ in $\widehat P$ if and only if there are a monomorphism $\iota_g:A_5\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and $u\in\overline L\leq\widehat P$ satisfying \[ \iota_g(t)=t\quad(t\in T),\qquad \iota_g(d)=g d g^{-1}\quad(d\in D),\qquad \iota_g(a)=u a u^{-1}\quad(a\in A_5). \] The monomorphism, when it exists, is unique from its first two prescriptions. For such a monomorphism, \[ g\in(H_T\cap L)H_5 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \iota_g=h\iota h^{-1}\text{ for some }h\in L. \] Consequently the refined closure condition in B.46 is exactly the following assertion, for all $L$ and $g$: every displayed homomorphism conjugacy realized in $\overline L$ is realized in $L$. This is simultaneous conjugacy of homomorphisms, with the restrictions on $T$ and $D$ retained.
answers: Part B.4(c) exact simultaneous finite-action conjugacy reduction
notes: Retains homomorphisms rather than subgroup conjugacy, pure labels, and every finite-index L. B.52 proves the unrefined case and B.58 every refinement containing [P,P]; arbitrary nonabelian finite levels remain unproved.

statement: Every nontrivial Sylow subgroup of the kernel is nonabelian Every nontrivial pro-$p$ Sylow subgroup of $\mathcal K$ is a free pro-$p$ group of rank at least two. Moreover $\mathcal K$ has no nontrivial closed abelian subgroup stable under the based $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$ action of B.31. In particular $Z(\mathcal K)=1$, and if $\mathcal K$ has finite derived length then $\mathcal K=1$. The last assertion concerns solvability with finite derived length; it does not exclude a nontrivial prosolvable group of unbounded derived length.
depends_on: B.29–B.32; full profinite Sylow conjugacy; free-pro-p criterion
notes: Each nonzero Sylow has rank≥2; centerK=1; finite derived length forcesK=1. Prosolvable of unbounded derived length is not excluded.

statement: Complex conjugation excludes the odd part and constrains odd Sylow normalizers Let $c\in G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$ be complex conjugation for the chosen real embedding. Then \[ C_{\widehat F_T}(c)=1,\qquad C_{\mathcal K}(c)=1. \tag{B.51.1} \] Every pro-odd closed subgroup of $\mathcal K$ stable under the based $G_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)}$ action is trivial. In particular a nontrivial $\mathcal K$ has a nonabelian pro-$2$ Sylow subgroup, and its largest closed normal pro-odd subgroup $O_{2'}(\mathcal K)$ is trivial. For every nontrivial odd-prime Sylow subgroup $S$ of $\mathcal K$, its geometric normalizer $N_{\mathcal K}(S)$ has a nontrivial pro-$2$ Sylow subgroup. If $S$ is finitely generated, then $C_{\mathcal K}(S)$ contains a nontrivial pro-$2$ subgroup. These assertions do not establish that $S$ has infinite rank.
depends_on: B.50; explicit realextension Zhat amalg C2; HR1985A′/B′; coprime fixed-point lifting
answers: B.4(f), Lead8: stronger actual-K restrictions and exact finite-rank bottleneck
notes: K nontrivial requires a nonabelian2-Sylow and O_2′(K)=1. Every odd Sylow normalizer has2-part; finite-rank odd Sylow forces nontrivial commutingpro2subgroup. General self-normalizer shortcut refuted by projective direct-product model, not an actualK example.

statement: The tetrahedral--cyclic product is a finite word-equation locus Let $\Gamma=\Gamma_{0,[12]}$, let $P$ be its pure subgroup, and retain the icosahedral embedding $\iota:A_5\hookrightarrow\Gamma$. Choose $T\cong A_4$ and $D=\langle d\rangle\cong C_5$ in $A_5$, and put $H_T=C_P(T)$ and $H_5=C_P(D)$. Then $H_TH_5$ is closed in the full profinite topology of $P$. The full centralizer product $C_\Gamma(T)C_\Gamma(D)$ is closed in the full profinite topology of $\Gamma$. So is $F_TF_5$ for the explicitly normalized rank-two subgroup $F_5$ constructed below, with $F_T=C_\Gamma(T)$ as in B.30. More precisely, choose generators $t_1,t_2$ of $T$ and any finite presentation \[ A_5=\langle t_1,t_2,d\mid\mathcal R\rangle. \] With these letters interpreted as the fixed elements of $\Gamma$, \[ H_TH_5 =\{g\in P:R(t_1,t_2,gdg^{-1})=1 \text{ for every }R\in\mathcal R\}. \tag{B.52.1} \] Consider embeddings $A_5\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ with the same elementwise permutation action as $\iota$ on the twelve punctures. They form exactly four $P$-conjugacy classes. A residue in $(\mathbb Z/5)^\times$ at one named $D$-fixed puncture distinguishes these four classes. These are the exact unrefined products proved for route B.4(c). It does not prove closure of all its finite-index refinements; the exact remaining obstruction is given below.
depends_on: B.7 (discrete normalizer); Stukow Theorem 4; Kerckhoff Theorem 5; Gonzalez-Meneses Section 2.2; residual finiteness of Gamma

Then \begin{align} C_R(a)&=\langle a\rangle\times \bigl(\mathbb Z^2(b,k)*F(CaC,CdC,CeC)\bigr), \label{eq:B116-centralizer-a}\\ C_R(aB)&=\langle aB\rangle\times F(b,CaC). \label{eq:B116-centralizer-prefix} \end{align} Both displayed cyclic factors are infinite. Their centralizer abelianizations have ranks six and three, respectively. Consequently no automorphism of $R$ sends $a$ to $aB$. In particular the actual prefix automorphism $\theta$ of the common free neck $K$ in B.115 extends to no discrete automorphism of $R$, with no restriction on the proposed image of $k$. This statement does not identify centralizers of these infinite-order elements in $\widehat R$. B.115 supplies the separate full profinite obstruction for homomorphisms whose image of $k$ is ordinary and has odd base winding. Neither statement transfers a regional nonmembership claim through the two actual cross relations.

statement: The actual regional boundary subgroup is a fully embedded profinite free product, with an exact discrete and completed neck intersection \label{stmt:B118} Use the actual annular regional marking of B.112--B.114, before the two additional cross relations. Write \[ B=CbC,\qquad z=Ch,\qquad f=hk^{-1}=Czk^{-1}, \qquad K=F(a,B,d,e,f)\leq R. \] Let $c=aCa^{-1}$ be the selected upper-gap cone, and put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-marked-boundary} P=P_5=O_1O_2O_3O_4O_5=aBfde,\qquad T=cP=abzde k^{-1},\qquad H=\langle c,k,T\rangle\leq R. \end{equation} Then the indicated generators give an isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-H} H\cong C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T), \end{equation} and $H$ has its full induced profinite topology in $R$. The actual neck intersection is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-intersections} K\cap H=\langle P\rangle,\qquad \widehat K\cap\widehat H =\overline{\langle P\rangle}\quad\text{inside }\widehat R. \end{equation} Here the hats are full profinite completions embedded by the proved induced-topology comparisons. The bar denotes the actual compact closure in $\widehat R$; it is the full procyclic completion of $\langle P\rangle$. There is also an auxiliary corner group \begin{equation}\label{eq:B118-corner} W_{\partial}= \langle D,u,k,j\mid D^2=j^2=1,\ [k,D]=[k,u]=1, \ juj=u^{-1}\rangle. \end{equation} The marked assignment $c\mapsto jDj$, $T\mapsto uD$, $k\mapsto k$ embeds the free product \eqref{eq:B118-H} in $W_{\partial}$, again with its full induced profinite topology. This is a comparison with the isolated corner: no embedding after the remaining regional or mirror relations, and no properness assertion for an additional profinite amalgam, is included in the theorem.
