statement: The actual one-neck ordinary group has a complete thirteen-generator presentation, and its eight-family filling has exactly the actual free-two fixed source in both full categories \label{stmt:B119} Let $\mathcal G=G_{\rm ann}$ be the actual orbifold group of B.114, over the two complete annuli joined through the first regular neck. Use its actual common disk marking $K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$, actual selected gap cones $c=c_-$ and $\tau=c_+$, and actual far-section loops $m=k_-$, $p=k_+$. Let $\mathcal G^0$ be the ordinary index-two subgroup: $c,\tau$ are odd and $K,m,p$ are even. Put \[ \widetilde u=cuc\quad(u=a,B,d,e,f),\qquad g=\widetilde f,\qquad x=\tau c. \] Then $\mathcal G^0$ has the following complete marked presentation: thirteen generators \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-thirteen} a,B,d,e,f,\ \widetilde a,\widetilde B,\widetilde d, \widetilde e,g,\ m,p,x, \end{equation} and the sixty-four regional relators specified by the explicit two-sheet rewriting scheme in the proof. The two cross commutators are eliminated by exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-cross-elimination} cmc=x^{-1}mx,\qquad cpc=p. \end{equation} No regional relator or signed base-loop consequence is discarded. Let $\mathcal N$ be the ordinary normal closure of the eight actual deleted-family meridians \[ a,B,d,e,\widetilde a,\widetilde B,\widetilde d,\widetilde e, \] and let $Q^0=\mathcal G^0/\mathcal N$ be the actual filling of both families. Then there is an exact marked isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-filled-semidirect} Q^0=F(f,g,x)\rtimes F(m,p), \end{equation} where conjugation by $m,p$ acts on the free fiber by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-base-actions} \begin{array}{c|ccc} &f&g&x\\ \hline \alpha_m&f^{-1}gf&f&xg^{-1}f\\ \alpha_p&fxgx^{-1}f^{-1}&gx^{-1}fxg^{-1}&fxg^{-1}. \end{array} \end{equation} The six actual positive source generators from B.114 map, in their actual order, to \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-source-images} 1,\ 1,\ 1,\ 1,\ v=f^{-1}p,\ m. \end{equation} Write $S=\langle m,v\rangle\leq Q^0$. Then $S\cong F_2$ is an actual source splitting of the geometric base projection, and conjugation $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$ satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-fixed-equalities} (Q^0)^\delta=S, \qquad (\widehat{Q^0})^\delta=\widehat S. \end{equation} All completions are full profinite completions, and $S$ has its full induced topology. Equivalently, for the filled orbifold group $Q=Q^0\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B119-orbifold-centralizers} C_Q(\tau)=S\times\langle\tau\rangle, \qquad C_{\widehat Q}(\tau)=\widehat S\times\langle\tau\rangle. \end{equation} These are assertions about the actual eight-family filling. They do not give a splitting back into $\mathcal G^0$, a fixed-element lift through $\mathcal N$, or a centralizer formula for the family-unfilled one-neck group.

statement: The actual boundary amalgam has a proper full completion, an exact discrete free-six cone centralizer, and a fully embedded carrier for the four remaining prefix relations \label{stmt:B120} Use the actual regional marking of B.112, B.114 and B.118. To distinguish the adapted cone from the selected upper-gap cone, write \[ \bar x=CxC,\quad B=CbC,\quad z=Ch,\quad f=hk^{-1},\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad c=aCa^{-1}. \] The actual physical neck basis and its prefixes are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-prefixes} \begin{gathered} (O_1,O_2,O_3,O_4,O_5) =(aBa^{-1},a,fde d^{-1}f^{-1},d,d^{-1}fd),\\ P_i=O_1\cdots O_i,\qquad P=P_5=aBfde,\qquad T=cP. \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular $P_1,\ldots,P_5$ are a free basis of the actual $K$. Let $R$ be the whole regional group, including every annular node relation and the retained zero-loop action. By B.118 its actual boundary subgroup is \[ H=\langle c,k,T\rangle=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T),\qquad K\cap H=\langle P\rangle, \] and $H$ and $K$ have their full induced topology in $R$, with $\widehat K\cap\widehat H=\overline{\langle P\rangle}$ there. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-corner-amalgam} \begin{split} W_{\partial}&=\langle D,u,k,j\mid D^2=j^2=1, \ [k,D]=[k,u]=1,\ juj=u^{-1}\rangle,\\ M&=R*_{H}W_{\partial}, \end{split} \end{equation} where the corner edge map is $c\mapsto jDj$, $T\mapsto uD$, and $k\mapsto k$. Both are the actual embedded edge maps of B.118. Then the full completion is a proper profinite amalgam: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-full-completion} \widehat M\cong \widehat R\amalg_{\widehat H}\widehat{W_{\partial}}. \end{equation} Here both vertex completions, and hence the indicated edge completion, inject. Let $L\cong F_5$ be the actual selected regional source in $R$, so that $C_R(c)=L\times\langle c\rangle$ by B.112 after the specified conjugation by $a$. With $k'=jkj$ one has the exact \emph{discrete} formulas \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-discrete-centralizers} \begin{aligned} C_M(c)&=(L*\langle k'\rangle)\times\langle c\rangle \cong F_6\times C_2,\\ C_M(D)&=(jLj*\langle k\rangle)\times\langle D\rangle. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The full actual mirror extension $X$ of the annular one-neck group is precisely \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-final-quotient} X=M/\langle\!\langle(jP_i)^2:\ 1\leq i\leq4\rangle\!\rangle. \end{equation} The four relations lie in the genuinely embedded subgroup \begin{equation}\label{eq:B120-carrier} J_0=\langle K,j\rangle =F(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)*C_2(j)*C_2(jP_5),\qquad w_i=jP_i. \end{equation} This carrier has its full induced topology in $M$, so its full completion also embeds in $\widehat M$. The six words identified below are actual source prelifts in the free factor of $C_M(D)$; their images under \eqref{eq:B120-final-quotient} are the six original based source words. Neither a centralizer formula in $\widehat M$ nor survival of these source generators after the four relations is asserted.

statement: The actual six-cone mirror neck is a retract of an original-parity index-two subgroup after all four final relations; its free-five neck is a retract in the ordinary annular group \label{stmt:B121} Keep the whole actual marking and intermediate group $M$ of B.120. In particular $C$ is the adapted regional cone, $c=aCa^{-1}$ is the selected gap cone, $K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$ with $B=CbC$, and $P_i=O_1\cdots O_i$ are the actual five prefixes. Let \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-actual-quotient} X=M/\langle\!\langle(jP_i)^2:\ 1\leq i\leq4\rangle\!\rangle, \qquad Q=K\rtimes_\eta C_2(j) =\mathop{*}_{i=0}^{5}C_2(r_i), \quad r_0=j,\ r_i=jP_i. \end{equation} The canonical homomorphism $\iota:Q\to X$ comes from the actual neck and mirror, with every remaining relation imposed. Let $\varepsilon:X\to C_2$ be the original ordinary-cover character, extended by $\varepsilon(j)=0$, so $\varepsilon(C)=1$ and it vanishes on the ordinary regional generators. Let $\mu:X\to C_2$ be mirror parity, zero on $R$ and one on $j$. Write \[ X^0=\ker\varepsilon,\qquad \Gamma=\ker\mu,\qquad \Gamma^0=\ker\mu\cap\ker\varepsilon. \] Thus $\Gamma$ is the actual annular one-neck orbifold group and $\Gamma^0$ is its actual ordinary double cover. The two characters are distinct. There is a literal retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-retractions} \mathcal R:X^0\longrightarrow Q, \qquad \mathcal R\iota=1_Q, \qquad \mu|_Q\circ\mathcal R=\mu|_{X^0}. \end{equation} In particular $\iota$ is injective. Restricting this retraction along mirror parity gives a retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-ordinary-neck-retract} \mathcal R|_{\Gamma^0}:\Gamma^0\longrightarrow K, \qquad \mathcal R|_K=1_K. \end{equation} Consequently $Q$ has its full induced profinite topology in $X$ and $K$ has its full induced profinite topology in $\Gamma^0$ and $\Gamma$. The natural full completions therefore embed: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B121-completed-embeddings} \widehat Q\hookrightarrow\widehat X, \qquad \widehat K\hookrightarrow\widehat{\Gamma^0} \hookrightarrow\widehat\Gamma. \end{equation} This is a statement about the actual final quotient. It does not assert that either regional vertex embeds after the final relations, or that the source image is free, or that a selected-cone centralizer is exhausted by the source.

statement: The selected-cone centralizer in the full completion of the intermediate boundary amalgam is exactly the closure of its actual discrete source centralizer \label{stmt:B122} Use the complete marked intermediate group of B.120, \[ M=R*_{H}W_{\partial},\qquad H=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T),\qquad c=aCa^{-1}, \] with the actual selected regional source $L\cong F_5$ and \[ \begin{gathered} W_{\partial}=\langle D,u,k,j\mid D^2=j^2=1, [k,D]=[k,u]=1,\ juj=u^{-1}\rangle,\\ c=jDj,\qquad T=uD,\qquad k'=jkj. \end{gathered} \] All completions below are full profinite completions embedded by the proved induced-topology comparisons. Closures are taken in $\widehat M$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B122-closure-centralizers} \begin{aligned} C_{\widehat M}(c) &=\overline{C_M(c)} =\overline{\langle L,k',c\rangle},\\ C_{\widehat M}(D) &=\overline{C_M(D)} =\overline{\langle jLj,k,D\rangle}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Thus the completed centralizer contains no elements beyond the closure of the actual discrete centralizer from B.120. This is a closure equality. It does not assert that the full completion of $F_6\times C_2$ embeds under its discrete centralizer map, or that the completed centralizer is a free profinite amalgam. The four remaining prefix relations defining the actual final group are not imposed in this statement.

statement: The whole ordinary one-neck group has an exact free-eleven, two-source-operator presentation, and its fixed-source question reduces to the actual family kernel in both categories \label{stmt:B123} Use the actual common marking of B.114 and B.119: \[ K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\qquad c=c_-,\qquad \tau=c_+,\qquad m=k_-,\quad p=k_+. \] The two cones are odd and the other generators are ordinary. Let \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-generic-fiber} E_0=K*C_2(c)*C_2(\tau),\qquad F=\ker(E_0\longrightarrow C_2). \end{equation} Then $F$ is the actual free group of rank eleven, with marked basis \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-free-eleven} a,B,d,e,f,\ cac,cBc,cdc,cec,g=cfc,\ x=\tau c. \end{equation} There are two explicitly specified automorphisms $\alpha_m,\alpha_v$ of $F$, defined below by the complete regional markings and partial inner automorphisms. There is a finite list $\mathcal A$ of \emph{forty} marked words, namely both ordinary sheets of all twenty regional node words. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-whole-closure} \begin{gathered} S=F(m,v),\qquad N=\left\langle\!\left\langle \alpha_s(r):r\in\mathcal A,\ s\in S \right\rangle\!\right\rangle_F,\qquad W=F/N. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here $s$ ranges over \emph{every signed word} in $m,v$, with $\alpha_s(w)=sws^{-1}$; no bound on its length is imposed. There is an exact marked isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-actual-splitting} \mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}=W\rtimes S. \end{equation} The actual fifth source word is $v$, and its sixth source word is $m$. The four contact source words give explicit elements $s_1,\ldots,s_4\in W$. Their full image is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-source-orbit} H=I\rtimes S,\qquad I=\left\langle\alpha_s(s_i):s\in S,\ 1\leq i\leq4\right\rangle \leq W. \end{equation} The brackets defining $I$ denote a subgroup, not an ambient normal closure. Conjugation $\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)$ preserves $W$ and fixes $S$ pointwise. Let $J=\ker(W\to F(f,g,x))$ be the actual eight-family filling kernel. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-discrete-gate} (\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann})^\delta=W^\delta\rtimes S, \qquad W^\delta=J^\delta,\qquad (\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann})^\delta=H \ \Longleftrightarrow\ J^\delta=I. \end{equation} There are also exact full-completion comparisons \begin{equation}\label{eq:B123-compact-gate} \begin{gathered} \widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}=\widehat W\rtimes\widehat S, \qquad \widehat W=\widehat F/\overline N,\qquad \overline H=\overline I\rtimes\widehat S,\\ \bigl(\widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}\bigr)^\delta =\widehat W^{\,\delta}\rtimes\widehat S, \qquad \widehat W^{\,\delta}=\overline J^{\,\delta},\\ \bigl(\widehat{\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}}\bigr)^\delta=\overline H \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \overline J^{\,\delta}=\overline I, \qquad \overline J=\ker\bigl(\widehat W\to\widehat{F(f,g,x)}\bigr). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here $\overline N$ is the closure of $N$ in $\widehat F$; $\overline I$ is the closure of the discrete actual source-orbit subgroup in $\widehat W$; and $\overline H$ is the image of the completed actual source. The notation $\overline J$ means the displayed actual closed kernel. No identification of it with $\widehat J$, or of $\overline N$ with $\widehat N$, is asserted. The equalities $J^\delta=I$ and $\overline J^{\,\delta}=\overline I$ remain open.

statement: The actual outer five-source factor is a retract after all final relations, and the complete actual source has free abelianization of rank six \label{stmt:B124} Let $\Gamma^0$ be the actual ordinary annular one-neck group of B.119--B.123, after all regional node, cross and prefix relations. Use its six based positive source loops \[ (s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,v,m) \] from B.123, with $s_i$ the four contact loops, $v$ the outer annular source loop and $m$ the inner source loop. Let \[ L_+=\langle s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,v\rangle,\qquad H_{\mathrm{src}}=\langle L_+,m\rangle\leq\Gamma^0. \] Then the displayed five generators freely generate $L_+\cong F_5$, and there is an actual retraction \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-source-retract} \rho_+:\Gamma^0\longrightarrow L_+, \qquad \rho_+(s_i)=s_i, \quad\rho_+(v)=v,\quad\rho_+(m)=1. \end{equation} In particular $L_+$ has its full induced profinite topology in $\Gamma^0$ and in the actual orbifold group $\Gamma$ containing $\Gamma^0$ with index two. Let $\iota:F_6\to\Gamma^0$ be the actual source map and let $p_{\mathrm{out}}:F_6\to F_5$ kill $m$, while $p_{\mathrm{base}}:F_6\to F(v,m)$ kills the four contacts. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-kernel-bounds} \ker\iota\subseteq\ker p_{\mathrm{out}}\cap\ker p_{\mathrm{base}}, \qquad \ker\widehat\iota\subseteq \ker\widehat p_{\mathrm{out}}\cap\ker\widehat p_{\mathrm{base}}. \end{equation} The second statement uses the actual map into $\widehat{\Gamma^0}$ and the full completions of the source free factors. If $\overline H_{\mathrm{src}}$ denotes the actual compact source image in $\widehat{\Gamma^0}$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B124-source-abelianization} H_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\mathbb Z^6, \qquad (\overline H_{\mathrm{src}})^{\mathrm{ab}}_{\mathrm{cont}} \cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,6}, \end{equation} with the indicated six source generators as basis. The continuous abelianization means quotient by the closed commutator subgroup. These statements do not assert injection of the entire $F_6$ or identify the actual compact source image with its abstract completion.

statement: The pre-cross ordinary cover is a proper full profinite star amalgam, and the actual cross filling is one specified commutator quotient \label{stmt:B125} Use the actual B.112--B.114 regional marking \[ R,\quad R^0=\ker\varepsilon_R,\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad B=CbC,\quad h=fk,\quad c=aCa^{-1}. \] Here $\varepsilon_R(C)=1$, every generator of $K$ and $k$ has ordinary parity zero, and $\eta$ is the actual based neck reflection. Put $Q=K\rtimes_\eta\langle j\rangle$, with $j^2=1$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-pre-cross} A=R*_{K}Q,\qquad X=A/\langle\!\langle[jcj,k]\rangle\!\rangle. \end{equation} Thus $X$ is the actual final mirror extension of B.114 and B.121; all regional relations and all five neck-prefix inversions are already present in $A$. Extend $\varepsilon_R$ to $\varepsilon:A\to C_2$ by killing $Q$, and write $A^0=\ker\varepsilon$. Let $j_0=j$, $j_1=CjC$, and $K_1=CKC$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-star} A^0=Q_0*_{K}R^0*_{K_1}Q_1, \qquad Q_0=Q,\quad Q_1=CQC. \end{equation} The two edge embeddings and all three vertex embeddings induce their full profinite topologies, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-completed-star} \widehat{A^0} =\widehat Q_0\amalg_{\widehat K}\widehat{R^0} \amalg_{\widehat K_1}\widehat Q_1 \end{equation} is a proper full profinite star amalgam. Define the actual words \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-single-words} \begin{gathered} a_1=CaC,\quad k_1=CkC,\quad t_0=j_0a a_1^{-1}j_1,\\ j'_0=a^{-1}j_0a,\quad j'_1=a_1^{-1}j_1a_1,\quad g=j'_0j'_1,\quad z_*=gh. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The original-parity character descends to $X$, and its kernel has the exact presentation \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-final-single} X^0=A^0/\langle\!\langle[z_*,k]\rangle\!\rangle_{A^0}. \end{equation} Here $z_*$ is the entire existing word in \eqref{eq:B125-single-words}, not a new free stable letter. The selected opposite cone is $\tau=jcj=t_0C$. The five exact selected regional source words $s_1,\ldots,s_5$ of B.120 give the actual six source prelifts \begin{equation}\label{eq:B125-source-prelifts} j_0s_1j_0,\ldots,j_0s_5j_0,k. \end{equation} Their images are the actual source words after the cross filling. The mirror character $\mu$ takes $j_0,j_1$ to $1$ and kills $R^0$; it is distinct from $\varepsilon$. The actual ordinary one-neck group is $X^0\cap\ker\mu$, and all words in \eqref{eq:B125-source-prelifts} lie in it. No vertex survival or selected-centralizer equality after \eqref{eq:B125-final-single} is asserted.

statement: The intermediate corner has the exact completed face, while the four final roots form a discrete malnormal cyclic family with sharp two-edge axis overlaps \label{stmt:B126} Use the actual intermediate amalgam of B.120: \[ M=R*_{H}W_\partial, \qquad H=\langle c,k,T\rangle=C_2(c)*\mathbb Z^2(k,T), \qquad P=P_5=cT. \] The corner satisfies $j^2=1$, $jPj=P^{-1}$ and $[jcj,k]=1$. Its mirror-even subgroup has the exact path presentation on $D,k,u,k',c$, with $D=jcj$, $k'=jkj$, $T=uD$, and edges $D$--$k$--$u$--$k'$--$c$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B126-corner-face} H\cap jHj=\langle P\rangle, \qquad \widehat H\cap j\widehat H j =\overline{\langle P\rangle} \quad\hbox{inside }\widehat W_\partial. \end{equation} The completed subgroups here are the actual full embedded completions from B.118--B.120. Let $\mathcal T_M$ be the ordinary Bass--Serre tree, let $e=H$ be its base edge, and for $1\leq i\leq4$ put \[ w_i=jP_i,\qquad \mathcal A_i=\operatorname{Axis}_{\mathcal T_M}(w_i). \] Each $w_i$ has translation length $2$. Distinct translates of these four axes intersect in at most two edges, and that bound is attained. Moreover \begin{equation}\label{eq:B126-axis-stabilizers} \operatorname{Stab}_M(\mathcal A_i) =C_M(w_i)=N_M(\langle w_i\rangle)=\langle w_i\rangle. \end{equation} The four cyclic groups form a malnormal family: if \[ \langle w_i\rangle\cap g\langle w_l\rangle g^{-1}\ne1, \] then $i=l$ and $g\in\langle w_i\rangle$. statement: The actual family kernel has an exact all-orbit Schreier presentation, a literal retained section, and a paired discrete abelianization \label{stmt:B127} Use the actual free-eleven presentation of B.123. Write \[ \mathcal U=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e) =(a,B,d,e,cac,cBc,cdc,cec),\qquad T=F(f,g,x), \] where \(g=cfc\), \(x=\tau c\), and bars exchange the two four-label halves. Thus \(F=F(\mathcal U)*T\). Let \(\pi:F\to T\) kill the eight family letters, let \(L=\ker\pi\), and let \(N\) be the entire defining normal subgroup of B.123, including every signed source translate of all forty marked ordinary node words. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-section} N\subseteq[L,L],\qquad J=L/N,\qquad W=F/N=J\rtimes T. \end{equation} The section of \(T\) is the literal subgroup on \(f,g,x\). It is a retained-fiber section, not a section of the whole coarse one-neck group into the unfilled group. The exact Schreier free basis of \(L\) is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-basis} X_{t,i}=tU_i t^{-1},\qquad t\in T,\quad U_i\in\mathcal U. \end{equation} The selected involution \(\delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau)\) acts on this entire basis by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-pairing} \delta(X_{t,i})=X_{\delta_T(t)x,\bar i},\qquad \delta_T(f)=xgx^{-1},\quad \delta_T(g)=xfx^{-1},\quad \delta_T(x)=x^{-1}. \end{equation} It is a fixed-point-free permutation of the basis. There is an exact discrete module identification \begin{equation}\label{eq:B127-ab} J_{\rm ab} =\bigoplus_{\substack{t\in T\\i\in\mathcal U}}\mathbb Z e_{t,i}, \qquad \delta(e_{t,i})=e_{\delta_T(t)x,\bar i}. \end{equation} In particular its Tate cohomology for this \(C_2\)-action vanishes in every degree. All nonlinear source corrections admit the uniform formula \eqref{eq:B127-nonlinear} below, and the exact relation subgroup is \eqref{eq:B127-L-closure}, with no cutoff on either source or retained-deck words. On actual full completions the retained section gives \[ \widehat W=\overline J\rtimes\widehat T,\qquad \overline J=\ker(\widehat W\to\widehat T). \] No equality \(\widehat J=\overline J\), no completed version of \eqref{eq:B127-ab}, and no lifting of invariant abelian classes to fixed group elements is asserted here.

statement: The continuous abelianization of the actual closed family kernel is a free completed group-ring module with paired involution, while the closed source has a proper image in its invariants \label{stmt:B128} Use the actual free presentation and full signed source orbit of B.123: \[ F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\qquad T=F(f,g,x),\qquad W=F/N, \] where the ordered family generators are \[ (U_1,\ldots,U_8)=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e), \qquad \bar U=cUc. \] Let $L=\ker(F\to T)$, $J=L/N$, and let $I\leq J$ be the actual source-family image generated by all signed source translates of the four contact words. In particular \[ \mathcal J=\ker(\widehat W\to\widehat T),\qquad \overline I\leq\mathcal J \] are actual closed subgroups, with no identification $\mathcal J=\widehat J$ assumed. Put \[ \Lambda_T=\widehat{\mathbb Z}[[\widehat T]], \qquad M=\Lambda_T^{\,8}. \] Then the literal retained section and family generators give a continuous $\widehat T$-module isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B128-actual-module} \mathcal J^{\mathrm{ab}}_{\mathrm{cont}}\cong M. \end{equation} The actual selected involution is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B128-module-involution} \delta(\lambda e_i)=\beta(\lambda)x e_{\bar i},\qquad \beta(f)=xgx^{-1},\quad\beta(g)=xfx^{-1},\quad\beta(x)=x^{-1}, \end{equation} where bar exchanges the two four-label sets and $\beta$ extends continuously to the completed group ring. As a compact additive $C_2$-module, $M$ is induced from four coefficient summands. Its continuous Tate groups vanish in every degree. Nevertheless the image of $\overline I$ in $M^\delta$ is proper. This is detected by the finite continuous quotient \begin{equation}\label{eq:B128-finite-detector} M\longrightarrow\bigl(\mathbb F_2[C_2]\bigr)^8 \end{equation} obtained by reducing coefficients modulo two and the retained $x$-exponent modulo two. In particular the invariant class \begin{equation}\label{eq:B128-missing-class} z=x e_a+e_{\bar a} \end{equation} is outside that source image. This statement concerns an abelian quotient. It neither supplies a fixed lift of $z$ in $\mathcal J$ nor decides $\mathcal J^\delta=\overline I$.

statement: A residue-three free-fiber quotient gives an actual equivariant free-two retract and proves nonlinear nonlifting in both categories \label{stmt:B129} Use \(F,L,N,W,J,T\) and \(\delta\) from B.123 and B.127. statement: The actual six-generator one-neck source map is noninjective in both categories, and its image contains an explicitly retracted copy of $\mathbb Z^2$ \label{stmt:B130} Let $\mathcal G=\mathcal G^0_{\rm ann}$ be the actual ordinary one-neck group of B.114, B.119 and B.123. Use its certified common marking $K=F(a,B,d,e,f)$ and selected plus gap cone $\tau$. Moreover $\langle U,m\rangle$ is an actual retract isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$ in $\mathcal G$ and in the actual source image $H$. Its closure in $\widehat{\mathcal G}$ is a continuous retract canonically isomorphic to $\widehat{\mathbb Z}^2$, and the same retraction restricts to the actual closed source image $\overline H$. These conclusions do not decide the equality of that source image with the selected fixed subgroup. There is also a specified nontrivial element in the selected centralizer of the actual intermediate full completion $\widehat M$ of B.120 which is killed by the final four-prefix filling. Thus this filling is noninjective on that completed intermediate centralizer; no embedding of an abstract $\widehat F_6$ into $\widehat M$ is needed.

statement: The corrected d-contact does not commute with the inner source loop, discretely or in the actual full completion \label{stmt:B131} Use the complete actual presentation of B.123 and the actual kernels of B.127--B.128: \[ \begin{gathered} F=F(U_1,\ldots,U_8)*T,\quad T=F(f,g,x),\quad L=\ker(F\to T),\\ W=F/N,\quad J=L/N,\quad \Gamma_0=W\rtimes S,\quad S=F(m,v). \end{gathered} \] The ordered family labels are $(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e)$, where $\bar U=cUc$. The normal subgroup $N$ includes all forty actual ordinary node seeds, all their signed source translates, and their full $F$-normal closure. Write $s_1,\ldots,s_4$ for the four actual source contact words of B.123, and put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B131-contact-basis} \begin{aligned} A_s&=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1},& B_s&=A_s^{-1}s_1^{-1}A_s,\\ D_s&=s_2s_1s_3^{-1}s_1^{-1}s_2^{-1},& E_s&=s_2^{-1}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B131-noncommutation} [m,D_s]\ne1\quad\hbox{in }\Gamma_0 \quad\hbox{and in }\widehat\Gamma_0. \end{equation} More precisely, there is a split epimorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:B131-free-retract} q:J\longrightarrow F(X,Y),\qquad X\longmapsto B,\quad Y\longmapsto x\bar d x^{-1} \quad\hbox{under its section}, \end{equation} which sends $[m,D_s]$ to $YX^{-1}Y^{-1}X$. There is a continuous split analogue from the \emph{actual} closed family kernel $\mathcal J=\ker(\widehat W\to\widehat T)$ onto $\widehat F(X,Y)$. No identification $\mathcal J=\widehat J$ is made. The word is detected by the order-eight group $\operatorname{UT}_3(\mathbb F_2)$. Let $H_5=\langle s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,m\rangle\leq\Gamma_0$. Its image under the actual one-sided filling is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B131-one-sided-group} P_1=\bigl(F(A_s,D_s)\times\mathbb Z_m\bigr)*F(B_s,E_s), \end{equation} and the induced epimorphism $H_5\to P_1$ is proper. If $E_5$ is the abstract free group on $A_s,B_s,D_s,E_s,m$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:B131-kernel-sandwich} \langle\!\langle[m,A_s]\rangle\!\rangle_{E_5} \ \subseteq\ \ker(E_5\to H_5) \ \subsetneq\ \langle\!\langle[m,A_s],[m,D_s]\rangle\!\rangle_{E_5}. \end{equation} No equality or strictness is asserted at the first inclusion. The specified failure of injectivity also holds for abstract full completions and for the actual closure map induced by the whole one-sided filling, without identifying subgroup completions with their ambient closures.

statement: The actual inner source loop and corrected d-contact generate a free group of rank two with its full profinite topology \label{stmt:B132} Use the actual ordinary group and complete relation family of B.123, B.127 and B.131: \[ \Gamma_0=W\rtimes S,\qquad S=F(m,v),\qquad W=F/N,\qquad F=F(\mathcal U)*T,\qquad T=F(f,g,x), \] where \(\mathcal U=(a,B,d,e,\bar a,\bar B,\bar d,\bar e)\). statement: The actual pre-cross six-source subgroup has its full profinite topology, and the final source kernels are specified ambient normal-closure intersections \label{stmt:B133} Use the actual B.112--B.125 marking \[ K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\qquad c=aCa^{-1},\qquad Q=K\rtimes_\eta\langle j\rangle,\qquad j^2=1, \] and the proper pre-cross amalgam and its actual cross quotient \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-pre-cross} A=R*_{K}Q,\qquad r_\times=[jcj,k],\qquad X=A/\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle_A. \end{equation} Here $R$ is the entire regional orbifold group, $R^0$ is its original ordinary subgroup, $\eta$ is the actual based neck reflection, and $k$ is the actual regional base loop. Let $S=\langle s_1,\ldots,s_5\rangle\leq R^0$ be the actual regional source group of B.112, with its entire selected-gap conjugations. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-source} \mathscr F=\langle js_1j,\ldots,js_5j,k\rangle\leq A. \end{equation} Then $\mathscr F=jSj*\langle k\rangle$ is free of rank six, and has its full induced profinite topology in $A$. In particular \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-free-completion} \widehat{\mathscr F}\ \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\ \widehat A, \qquad \overline{\mathscr F}^{\,\widehat A} =j\widehat Sj\amalg\overline{\langle k\rangle} \cong\widehat F_6, \end{equation} where the factors are the actual closures of the specified source words and base loop. Let $\Gamma_0$ be the actual ordinary one-neck subgroup of $X$, the joint kernel of the original and mirror characters. All six words in \eqref{eq:B133-source} map into $\Gamma_0$. Define \[ N_\times=\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle_A, \qquad \mathcal N_\times= \overline{\langle\!\langle r_\times\rangle\!\rangle}^{\,\widehat A}. \] With the embedding in \eqref{eq:B133-free-completion}, the exact discrete and compact source kernels are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B133-kernel-intersections} \begin{aligned} \ker(\mathscr F\longrightarrow\Gamma_0) &=\mathscr F\cap N_\times,\\ \ker(\widehat{\mathscr F}\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_0) &=\widehat{\mathscr F}\cap\mathcal N_\times. \end{aligned} \end{equation} These are intersections with the actual ambient normal closures. No equality between the closure of the first kernel and the second kernel is asserted. The theorem does not assert injectivity of the final six-source map, whose nonzero kernel was exhibited in B.130, or identify its full internal normal-generating family.

statement: Both mirror sheets give an exact edge pushout, an ordinary kernel-matching closure, and an independent finite matching-normal criterion \label{stmt:B134} Use the actual ordinary pre-cross star of B.125, with $j_0=j$, $j_1=CjC$, $K_1=CKC$ and $p=\operatorname{Ad}(j_0)$. The kernel of mirror parity in that star has the proper presentation \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-pre-HNN} \begin{gathered} V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0),\qquad p(u)=\eta(u)\quad(u\in K),\qquad t=j_0j_1,\\ \langle V,t\mid tut^{-1}=\sigma(u)\ (u\in K_1)\rangle, \qquad \sigma(CuC)=p(C\eta(u)C)\quad(u\in K). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Let $\theta=\operatorname{Ad}(j_0)$ on $V$; it interchanges the two vertex groups, and on the pre-cross HNN group sends $t$ to $t^{-1}$. Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-actual-words} \begin{gathered} a_1=CaC,\quad k_1=CkC,\quad f_1=CfC,\\ v_0=p(aa_1^{-1}),\quad w_0=\theta(v_0)=aa_1^{-1},\\ s=v_0^{-1}kv_0,\qquad s'=w_0^{-1}p(k)w_0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Then the actual final ordinary one-neck group is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-two-cross-presentation} \begin{gathered} \Gamma_0=\langle V,t\mid tut^{-1}=\sigma(u)\ (u\in K_1),\\ tk_1t^{-1}=s,\quad ts't^{-1}=p(k_1)\rangle. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Both last equations are required. Let $E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C$ be the actual B.117 subgroup, and set \[ (u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) =\bigl(CaC,CdC,CeC,C(f^{-1}Bf)C\bigr). \] Its exact presentation is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-E1} E_1=\langle f_1,k_1,u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4\mid [(f_1k_1)^2,k_1],\ [k_1,u_i]\ (1\leq i\leq4)\rangle. \end{equation} Define the five target words in $V$ by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-rhos} \rho_0=[(\sigma(f_1)s)^2,s],\qquad \rho_i=[s,\sigma(u_i)]\quad(1\leq i\leq4). \end{equation} Put \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-initial-quotient} \begin{gathered} N_* =\langle\!\langle\rho_i,\theta(\rho_i) \ (0\leq i\leq4)\rangle\!\rangle_V, \qquad V_*=V/N_*,\\ E=E_1*\langle y\rangle. \end{gathered} \end{equation} There are genuine homomorphisms $i,j:E\to V_*$ defined on $E_1$ by its actual inclusion and by $(K_1,k_1)\mapsto (\sigma(K_1),s)$, respectively, and on the extra generator by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-extra-edge} i(y)=s',\qquad j(y)=p(k_1). \end{equation} Neither map is presumed injective. With these maps, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-pushout} \Gamma_0=\langle V_*,t\mid ti(e)t^{-1}=j(e)\ (e\in E)\rangle. \end{equation} Define normal subgroups of $V_*$ by \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-saturation} \begin{split} M_0&=1,\\ M_{n+1}&=\langle\!\langle M_n,\ i(j^{-1}(M_n)),\ j(i^{-1}(M_n))\rangle\!\rangle_{V_*},\\ M_\infty&=\bigcup_{n\geq0}M_n. \end{split} \end{equation} Then $V_*/M_\infty$ embeds in \eqref{eq:B134-pushout} as the base of a proper ordinary HNN extension. In particular \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-discrete-base-kernel} \ker(V_*\longrightarrow\Gamma_0)=M_\infty. \end{equation} No finite stabilization is asserted. Independently, let $\mathcal B$ consist of the finite-index normal subgroups $N\triangleleft V_*$ satisfying $i^{-1}(N)=j^{-1}(N)$. Their associated open normal subgroups of $\widehat V_*$ give the exact compact criterion \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-compact-base-kernel} \ker(\widehat V_*\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma_0) =\bigcap_{N\in\mathcal B}\overline N^{\,\widehat V_*}. \end{equation} Every such $N$ is the exact restriction of a finite quotient kernel of $\Gamma_0$. Equality of the right side with $\overline{M_\infty}^{\,\widehat V_*}$ is not inferred. Finally the one actual source commutation of B.130, even together with its mirror, does not suffice for this edge regrouping. If \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-known-U} U=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1} =a v_0\sigma(a_1)v_0^{-1}\in V, \end{equation} then the three words $\rho_2,\rho_3,\rho_4$ remain nontrivial in \begin{equation}\label{eq:B134-one-source-repair} V/\langle\!\langle[k,U],\theta([k,U])\rangle\!\rangle_V. \end{equation} They are not identified here with commutators of the corrected $D_s$ or $E_s$ source coordinates.

statement: The actual whole group has a marked inner-star relative presentation whose base map is noninjective in both categories; on an explicit retract block its kernel and the new source fixed subgroup are exact \label{stmt:B135} Use the actual one-neck marking and source operators of B.123. In the minus local tuple write \[ E_0=C_2(C)*F(a,b,d,e,f)*C_2(\tau),\qquad \delta=\operatorname{Inn}(\tau),\qquad a^*=\tau a\tau. \] The original orientation sends both cones to one in $C_2$ and all five ordinary letters, and both source letters $m,v$, to zero. Let $\Gamma_0$ be the actual ordinary group, and put $E_{\rm act}=\Gamma_0\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle$. All tuples, node words and operators used below are specified by finite word formulas in the proof. Let $R_-$ be the actual minus annular vertex, including its ten node relations and their full $m$-orbit. Before the remaining plus filling, the actual marked presentation is the proper amalgam \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-inner-star} G_{\rm in}=R_-*_{\langle m\rangle} (\langle m\rangle\times C_2(\tau)). \end{equation} Its selected-cone centralizers, discretely and after full completion, are \[ C_{G_{\rm in}}(\tau)=\langle m\rangle\times\langle\tau\rangle, \qquad C_{\widehat G_{\rm in}}(\tau) =\overline{\langle m\rangle}\times\langle\tau\rangle. \] Thus the entire original ordinary inner subgroup has fixed subgroup $\langle m\rangle$, and its actual full completion has fixed subgroup $\overline{\langle m\rangle}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. If $\beta$ is the actual $v$-operator and $\mathcal R_+$ the ten actual plus orbifold node words, the \emph{whole} actual group is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-whole-relative} E_{\rm act}= \left\langle G_{\rm in},v\ \middle|\ v yv^{-1}=\beta(y)\ (y=a,b,d,e,f,C,\tau),\quad \mathcal R_+\right\rangle . \end{equation} In particular this presentation retains all signed source translates of both node families, as well as every fiber conjugate. It does not assert that $\beta$ descends to an automorphism of $G_{\rm in}$. The element \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-killed-word} w=[a,a^*]=a\tau a\tau a^{-1}\tau a^{-1}\tau \end{equation} is nontrivial in $G_{\rm in}$ and in its full completion, but maps to one in $E_{\rm act}$ and its full completion. These noninjectivity assertions also hold on the original ordinary index-two subgroup and its full completion. The following sharper comparison concerns actual subgroup blocks. There are retractions onto \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-blocks} \begin{gathered} B=\langle a,\tau,m\rangle\leq G_{\rm in},\qquad B\cong(\mathbb Z(a)*C_2(\tau))\times\mathbb Z(m),\\ Q=\langle a,\tau,m\rangle\leq E_{\rm act},\qquad Q\cong(\mathbb Z^2(a,a^*)\rtimes_{\rm swap}C_2(\tau)) \times\mathbb Z(m). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Writing $B_0=B\cap G_{\rm in}^0$ and $Q_0=Q\cap\Gamma_0$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-block-kernels} \begin{gathered} B_0=F(a,a^*)\times\mathbb Z(m),\qquad Q_0=\mathbb Z^3(a,a^*,m),\\ \ker(B\to E_{\rm act})=\langle\!\langle w\rangle\!\rangle_B, \qquad \ker(B_0\to\Gamma_0)=\langle\!\langle w\rangle\!\rangle_{B_0}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Each displayed subgroup has its full induced profinite topology in the indicated ambient group. The corresponding kernels on their actual completed closures are precisely the closed normal closures of $w$. The retraction $\Gamma_0\to Q_0$ is $\delta$-equivariant. For the corrected actual contact $A_s=s_1s_4^{-1}s_1^{-1}$ of B.130, the fixed subgroups on this block are exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B135-fixed-creation} \begin{gathered} B_0^\delta=\langle m\rangle,\qquad (\widehat B_0)^\delta=\overline{\langle m\rangle},\\ Q_0^\delta=\langle aa^*,m\rangle =\langle A_s,m\rangle\cong\mathbb Z^2,\qquad (\widehat Q_0)^\delta =\overline{\langle A_s,m\rangle}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,2}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Thus the filling creates this known source fixed norm. These statements do not determine the whole kernel of $G_{\rm in}\to E_{\rm act}$ or the full fixed subgroup of $\Gamma_0$ or $\widehat\Gamma_0$.

statement: The unfilled inclusion edge embeds, its target contains a full free-six subgroup, and the proper local filling has an explicit fixed-point-free involution \label{stmt:B136} Use the actual B.134 marking \[ V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0),\quad K=F(a,B,d,e,f),\quad K_1=CKC, \quad L=\langle K,k\rangle,\quad E_1=CLC, \] where $p|_K=\eta$ and $\theta$ interchanges the two vertices. The inclusion-side map of the abstract B.134 edge \[ i_0:E=E_1*\langle y\rangle\longrightarrow V, \qquad i_0|_{E_1}=\mathrm{id},\quad i_0(y)=s' \] is injective. Its mirror is the embedded group \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-two-edges} \theta i_0(E)=\langle p(E_1),s\rangle=p(E_1)*\langle s\rangle. \end{equation} The actual subgroup \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-target-free} T_6=\langle\sigma(K_1),s\rangle =\sigma(K_1)*\langle s\rangle\cong F_6 \end{equation} has its full induced profinite topology in $V$. No full-topology assertion for $i_0(E)$ is inferred merely from its ordinary embedding. Write $\eta_1=\operatorname{Ad}(C)\eta\operatorname{Ad}(C)$ on $K_1$, and put \[ (u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) =\bigl(CaC,CdC,CeC,C(f^{-1}Bf)C\bigr). \] In $F_*=K_1*\langle k_1\rangle*\langle y\rangle$ let \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-local-relators} \mathcal R= \bigl\{[(f_1k_1)^2,k_1],\ [k_1,u_i]\ (1\leq i\leq4)\bigr\}. \end{equation} The automorphism $\kappa_0$ of $F_*$ acts by $\eta_1$ on $K_1$ and exchanges $k_1,y$. It is an involution. The group \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-Dloc} D_{\mathrm{loc}} =F_*/\langle\!\langle\mathcal R,\kappa_0(\mathcal R) \rangle\!\rangle \end{equation} is a proper ordinary amalgam of two copies of $E_1$ over $K_1$, with the second edge marking twisted by $\eta_1$. It has a proper full profinite amalgam completion and full vertex topologies. The induced involution $\kappa$ satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-fixed} D_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\kappa}=1, \qquad (\widehat D_{\mathrm{loc}})^{\kappa}=1. \end{equation} Let $V_*=V/N_*$ be the actual B.134 quotient by all five $\rho_i$ and their five $\theta$-mates. There is an actual map $a_{\mathrm{loc}}:D_{\mathrm{loc}}\to V_*$, and the other edge map is \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-two-maps} b_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta a_{\mathrm{loc}}\kappa. \end{equation} Replacing $E$ by $D_{\mathrm{loc}}$ in B.134's pushout does not change the actual group. Its initial ordinary kernel-matching condition is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-kernel-test} \ker a_{\mathrm{loc}}\text{ is }\kappa\text{-invariant}. \end{equation} The matching finite-index normal subgroups of $V_*$ may be chosen $\theta$-invariant cofinally. For such a subgroup $N$, the finite matching condition is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:B136-finite-test} a_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}(N)\text{ is }\kappa\text{-invariant}. \end{equation} Neither \eqref{eq:B136-kernel-test} nor an embedding of $D_{\mathrm{loc}}$ in $V_*$ is asserted. The fixed-subgroup statement \eqref{eq:B136-fixed} is strictly local.

statement: The two actual unfilled edge groups have trivial ordinary intersection, by exact vertex and incident-direction comparisons \label{stmt:B137} Use the actual unfilled B.134/B.136 amalgam $V=R^0*_{K}p(R^0)$, with $p|_K=\eta$ and its vertex-exchanging involution $\theta$. Put $E_1=C\langle K,k\rangle C$ and \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-edge-groups} \begin{gathered} H_i=\langle E_1,s'\rangle =\langle E_1,a^{-1}p(k)a\rangle,\\ H_j=\theta(H_i)=\langle p(E_1),s\rangle =\langle p(E_1),\eta(a)^{-1}k\eta(a)\rangle,\\ B_i=\langle f,a^{-1}p(k)a\rangle\leq p(R^0),\qquad B_j=\langle\eta(f),\eta(a)^{-1}k\eta(a)\rangle\leq R^0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The two displayed equalities retain the actual B.134 words $w_0=aa_1^{-1}$, $v_0=p(w_0)$, $s'=w_0^{-1}p(k)w_0$, $s=v_0^{-1}kv_0$, and $a_1=CaC$. There are embedded ordinary subamalgams \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-subamalgams} H_i=E_1*_{\langle f\rangle}B_i,\qquad H_j=B_j*_{\langle\eta(f)\rangle}p(E_1). \end{equation} Their standard vertex and edge intersections are \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-standard-intersections} \begin{gathered} H_i\cap R^0=E_1,\quad H_i\cap p(R^0)=B_i,\quad H_i\cap K=\langle f\rangle,\\ H_j\cap R^0=B_j,\quad H_j\cap p(R^0)=p(E_1),\quad H_j\cap K=\langle\eta(f)\rangle. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The actual vertex overlaps are trivial: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-overlaps} E_1\cap B_j=1,\qquad p(E_1)\cap B_i=1. \end{equation} In fact their whole ordinary intersection is trivial: \begin{equation}\label{eq:B137-whole-intersection} H_i\cap H_j=1. \end{equation} This conclusion uses the additional incident-direction comparison proved below, not just the two standard vertex stabilizers. No completed intersection, free-product assertion for the generated overgroup, or survival after the two local fillings is inferred.

statement: A nontrivial pro-odd kernel in a projective group cannot be small Let $B$ be a closed subgroup of a free profinite group. Suppose that \[ 1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow B \xrightarrow{\chi}\widehat{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow1 \] is exact. For every prime $p$, the group $K^{(p)}$ is either trivial or an infinitely generated free pro-$p$ group. Consequently, if $K$ is pro-odd and nontrivial, it has an infinitely generated free pro-$p$ quotient for some odd prime $p$. In particular such a $K$ is not topologically finitely generated. If $K$ is abelian, then $K=1$, without any pro-odd assumption.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The coarse structural data of LM4 D.78 do not force its kernel to vanish There is a two-generated projective profinite group $B$, embedded as a retract of $\widehat F_2$, with a split epimorphism $\chi:B\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ such that \[ B^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z},\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(B_0,\mathbb F_2)=1 \quad\text{for every open }B_0\leq B, \] but $\ker\chi$ is a nontrivial pro-$3$ group. Thus projectivity, these mod-two ranks, and the split pro-odd-kernel description alone do not imply $\ker\chi=1$. This is not an example of a torus involution or a refutation of the actual question C.1 of the prompt.
notes: Counterexample to inference only; not a realization as the actual torus fixed subgroup.

statement: The exact finite-coefficient witness for the actual torus kernel Let $E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle$ be the full negative torus extension of LM4 D.78, and let $T=\langle w\rangle$ be its noncusp section class. Suppose that the actual fixed subgroup $B=C_F(w)$ has the split epimorphism $\chi:B\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ of that row, with specified section $t\mapsto a^t$, and set $A=\overline{\langle a\rangle}$, $K=\ker\chi$. For a finite continuous left $E$-set $X$, put $Q_X=\mathbb F_2[X^T]$, with the induced $B$-action. Then \[ K=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Q_X^B\longrightarrow Q_X^A\text{ is onto for every such }X. \tag{C.3.1} \] If $1\ne k\in K$, one can take $X=E/(ATN)$, where $N$ is an open normal subgroup of $E$ contained in $F$ and chosen so that $k\notin ATN$. The identity-coset basis vector is an explicit witness to failure of surjectivity.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The actual kernel in prompt C.1 In the actual torus setting of C.3, prove or refute $K=1$. The audited structural conclusions of LM4 D.78 imply that $K$ is pro-odd. C.1 shows that any counterexample must have an infinitely generated free pro-$p$ quotient for an odd prime. It would suffice to prove that the actual $K$ is finitely generated, or that it is abelian. Neither assertion is established here. C.2 shows exactly why the abstract projectivity and mod-two rank arguments do not establish either assertion. The extra peripheral duality of the torus extension has not been realized in the countermodel of C.2.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: Primitive-homology centralizers and the original torus cusp If $F$ is free profinite and $a\in F$ admits a continuous character $\rho:F\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ with $\rho(a)=1$, then, for every nonzero integer $n$, \[ C_F(a^n)=N_F(\overline{\langle a\rangle}) =\overline{\langle a\rangle}\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \tag{C.5.1} \] For $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ and $c=[x,y]$, one also has $C_F(c)=N_F(\overline{\langle c\rangle})=\overline{\langle c\rangle}$. The first assertion requires primitive homology, not membership in a free basis.
depends_on: cohomological dimension one; finite Heisenberg quotients
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The finite-coefficient duality behind LM4 D.74--D.78 Let $(F;L_1,\ldots,L_m)$ be the full completion of an oriented compact surface with nonempty boundary and negative Euler characteristic. Let $E=F\rtimes C_2$ preserve each peripheral conjugacy class with exponent $-1$, and suppose $D_j=N_E(L_j)=L_j\rtimes_{-1}C_2$. Put $k=\mathbb F_2$, let $u:E\to k$ be the quotient character, and define \[ \Delta=\ker\left(\bigoplus_j k[[E/D_j]]\longrightarrow k\right), \qquad \mathscr H_M=\operatorname{Hom}_{k,\mathrm{cont}}(\Delta,M). \] For every finite continuous $E$-module $M$, absolute cohomology with coefficient $M$ and relative cohomology with coefficient $M^\vee$ have a natural perfect pairing after localization by $u$. For self-dual $M$, the localized boundary restriction has half the target rank: \[ \operatorname{rank}\left( H^\bullet(E,M)[u^{-1}]_0\longrightarrow \bigoplus_jH^\bullet(D_j,M)[u^{-1}]_0\right) =\frac12\sum_j\dim H^\bullet(D_j,M)[u^{-1}]_0. \tag{C.6.1} \] The subscript zero denotes degree zero after localization. The relative groups here use the original peripheral normalizers.
answers: C.4: LM4 D.74 and D.78 duality input
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The full pants section centralizers in LM4 D.74 For the normalized involution and three section classes of R1, every section has trivial centralizer in the full $F=\widehat F(x,y)$. Thus $N_E(S_i)=S_i$ for all three classes. The equation $f=h^{-1}\alpha(h)$ has exactly one solution in $F$, and that solution lies in $F'$. The extension $E=F\rtimes_\alpha C_2$ is real projective. If $\alpha\in\widehat{GT}_0$, the unique solution also satisfies $h\theta(h)=1$, where $\theta$ exchanges $x,y$.
depends_on: R1 (refereed); C.5–C.6; KZ 2007 Theorem 2; Haran 1993 Proposition 2.2
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: Negative torus section counts, cusp fusion and the centralizer in LM4 D.75 Let an outer involution of $F=\widehat F(x,y)$ preserve the commutator cusp $c=[x,y]$ with full multiplier $-1$. Its centre-free extension has a cusp-normalized splitting \[ E=F\rtimes\langle v\rangle, \qquad v^2=1,\qquad vcv^{-1}=c^{-1}. \] Write $A_2$ for its action on $H_1(F,\mathbb Z_2)$. If $A_2\not\equiv I\pmod2$ there is one section class and its geometric centralizer is trivial. If $A_2\equiv I\pmod2$ there are two classes: the cusp class has trivial geometric centralizer and the other has $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(C_F(w),\mathbb F_2)=1$. The two local cusp reflection classes are globally fused. In particular there is a unique $g\in F$ with $gvg^{-1}=cv$.
depends_on: C.5–C.6; KZ 2007 Theorem 2; specified global multiplier −1; C.18 proves global sign from dyadic sign
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The specified section augmentation module in LM4 D.76 In the pants extension of C.7 choose one actual section $T_i=\langle t_i\rangle$ from each class, and put $R=\mathbb F_2[[E]]$. Then the compact left module \[ \Delta_T=\ker\left(\bigoplus_{i=0}^2 \mathbb F_2[[E/T_i]]\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2\right) \] is isomorphic to $R^2$. For each finite $E$-module $M$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_E(\Delta_T,M)=2\dim M$. For the specified identity-coset vectors $e_i$ and $H=\overline{\langle T_0,T_1,T_2\rangle}$, the distinct incidence map satisfies \[ \begin{split} d_T:R^2&\longrightarrow\Delta_T, \quad(r_1,r_2)\longmapsto r_1(e_1-e_0)+r_2(e_2-e_0),\\ \operatorname{coker}d_T&\cong \ker\bigl(\mathbb F_2[[E/H]]\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2\bigr). \end{split} \tag{C.9.1} \] Thus $d_T$ is invertible exactly when the chosen sections generate $E$; freeness of $\Delta_T$ alone does not imply that conclusion.

statement: The proper three-section example of LM4 D.77 In the full profinite free product $E_0=C_2(a)\amalg C_2(b)\amalg C_2(d)$ put \[ x=ba,\quad y=da,\quad \delta=\operatorname{Ad}(a),\quad g=x[x,y]x^{-1},\quad Y=g y\delta(g)^{-1}. \] The orientation kernel is $F_0=\widehat F(x,y)$. The sections $a,b,gdg^{-1}$ represent its three section classes, yet generate a proper closed subgroup $H<E_0$. Its orientation kernel is $K=\overline{\langle x,Y\rangle}<F_0$, although its image in every $F_0^{(p)}$ is full. The incidence cokernel of C.9 has a five-dimensional finite quotient. The element $Y$ is not conjugate to any unit power of $y$.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The original negative transporter is homologically primitive In C.8 the transporter $g$ has primitive abelianization and generates the full fixed line of $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$. In the two-class case put $B=C_F(w)$ for the other section. Its homology image is exactly that line. There is a continuous epimorphism $\chi:E\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ with $\chi(g)=1$ and $\chi(B)=\widehat{\mathbb Z}$; one can choose $a\in B$ with $[a]=[g]$. Killing all torsion in $E$ gives precisely this torsion-free quotient. In the one-class case the torsion-free quotient is also $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, but its primitive character takes $g$ to $2$.

statement: The exact pro-odd-kernel conclusions of LM4 D.78 In the two-class situation of C.11, retain its actual $B=C_F(w)$, $T=\langle w\rangle$, $\chi$ and chosen $a\in B$. Put $A=\overline{\langle a\rangle}$ and $K=\ker(\chi|_B)$. Then \[ \dim H^1(B_0,\mathbb F_2)=1\quad(B_0\leq B\text{ open}), \qquad B=K\rtimes A, \qquad A\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}, \tag{C.12.1} \] and $K$ is pro-odd. For every finite two-primary $B$-module $Q$, inflation gives \[ H^n(\widehat{\mathbb Z},Q^K)\cong H^n(B,Q), \tag{C.12.2} \] and restriction to $A$ is the map induced by $Q^K\hookrightarrow Q$, with $t$ acting on $Q$ as $a^t$. The invariant-surjectivity criterion is exactly C.3, and remains additional to these conclusions.

statement: The exact transporter and conjugacy reduction of LM4 D.75 For $\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$ and $i\in\{0,1\}$ put $v_i=c^iv$. The unique solution of $[a,v_i]=c^\mu$ is \[ a_{\mu,0}=c^{(\mu-1)/2}g, \qquad a_{\mu,1}=c^{(\mu+1)/2}g^{-1}. \tag{C.13.1} \] The full peripheral conjugacy to the corresponding standard negative torus involution is equivalent to \[ \exists\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\ i\in\{0,1\}: c^{-\mu}a_{\mu,i}\sim_F a_{\mu,i}. \tag{C.13.2} \] Existence in (C.13.2) is not asserted.

statement: The existence requested by prompt C.2 For every negative involution of the full punctured-torus loop-outer group, does (C.13.2) have a solution? C.8 and C.13 prove uniqueness of every individual commutator transporter and all claimed equivalences in LM4 D.75. They do not supply the additional conjugacy. An outside element in $C_E(a_{\mu,i})$ would solve it; absence of such elements for all full units and both parity labels would refute it. The equation remains a full profinite conjugacy problem, and generation in each maximal pro-$p$ quotient does not solve it, as C.10 illustrates for the related section-generation problem.

statement: Prime-order lifting and full closed-surface primary faithfulness Every outer action of $C_p$ on the full free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ has an actual order-$p$ representative if its outer image has order $p$. For the full completed closed surface group $\Pi=\widehat{\pi_1(S_g)}$, $g\geq2$, the map \[ \operatorname{Aut}(\Pi)\longrightarrow \operatorname{GL}(H_1(\Pi,\mathbb Z_p)) \tag{C.15.1} \] is injective on finite $p$-subgroups. This second assertion concerns actual automorphisms, not outer automorphisms.

statement: The order-three assertion of LM4 D.42 Every element of order three in the full three-cusp loop-outer group allowing cusp permutations has multiplier $1\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$.

statement: The primary fixed-group and cusp arguments needed for the quartic audit Let $a$ be an actual automorphism of order $p$ of a full free profinite group $F_r$ which induces the identity on $F_r^{(p)}$. Then $F_r\rtimes_a C_p$ has one $F_r$-conjugacy class of sections, and restriction gives \[ H^1(F_r,\mathbb F_p)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^1(C_{F_r}(a),\mathbb F_p). \tag{C.17.1} \] If $F_r$ is the group of a sphere with $r+1\geq3$ cusps and $a$ preserves each cusp class with $p$-adic multiplier one, then $a=1$. If $r=2$ and $a$ preserves the torus cusp, the same conclusion holds. In particular the homology representation of the full torus loop-outer group is injective on each finite $p$-subgroup at its $p$-adic coordinate.

statement: The global torus involution sign, with the Heisenberg comparison specified Every involution of the full torus loop-outer group has multiplier equal to its global dyadic sign, $1$ or $-1$. This proves the upstream sign assertion LM4 D.43 used in the negative-involution and quartic calculations.

statement: Positive torus sections, full primary square, and actual quartic lifting A positive torus involution acts as $-I$ on $H_1(F,\mathbb Z_p)$ for every prime $p$. Its centre-free full extension has three kernel-conjugacy classes of sections, each with $H^1(C_F(S),\mathbb F_2)=0$. Its cusp normalizer is torsion-free, and a labelled cusp lift $v$ satisfies $v^2=c^\kappa$ with $\kappa_2$ a unit. Every order-four outer torus action has an actual order-four lift. For such an action, $A_p^2=-I$ at every prime, $\lambda^2=1$, and $\lambda_2=1$. These are precisely the portions of LM4 D.46 and D.55 needed below.

notes: Full versus pro-p comparison maps retained.

statement: The actual dihedral quotient behind the quartic argument Let $\alpha$ be the actual quartic torus representative of C.19, $c=[X,Y]$, and $E=F\rtimes\langle s\rangle$. There is a unique nonzero invariant character $\chi:F\to C_2$. One can choose a discrete free basis $x,y$, with $[x,y]=c$, $\chi(x)=1$, $\chi(y)=0$, such that the full quotient \[ F/\overline{\langle\!\langle x^2,(xy)^2\rangle\!\rangle} =\widehat{\mathbb Z}\rtimes C_2 =\langle r,t\mid t^2=1,\ trt=r^{-1}\rangle, \qquad x\mapsto t,\quad y\mapsto r \tag{C.20.1} \] is $\alpha$-invariant. The induced action is \[ \bar\alpha(r)=r^{-\lambda},\quad \bar\alpha(t)=r^jt,\quad (1-\lambda)j=0, \quad j_2\in\mathbb Z_2^\times. \tag{C.20.2} \] At every negative odd coordinate $q$, this gives a specified quotient $\rho:F\to D_{2q}$ with $\rho\alpha=\rho$, $\rho(c)=r^{-2}$, and $q\equiv1\pmod4$. This independently proves the portion of LM4 D.68 needed for D.70.

statement: The integral square on the nontrivial rotation summand Use a negative coordinate and the specified quotient of C.20. Put $N=\ker\rho$, $R=\langle r\rangle\cong C_q$, $\beta=\alpha^2$, $\sigma=s^2$, $C=C_F(\sigma)$ and $C_0=C\cap N$. Then \[ \rho(C)=R,\qquad \dim H^1(C_0,\mathbb F_2)=q-1. \tag{C.21.1} \] The cover $N$ has type $(q,2)$. If $V_2=H^1(N,\mathbb Z_2)$, $e=q^{-1}\sum_{r'\in R}r'$ and $W_2=(1-e)V_2$, then \[ \operatorname{rank}W_2=2(q-1),\qquad \beta^*|_{W_2}=I. \tag{C.21.2} \] There are two section classes in $N\rtimes\langle\sigma\rangle$, represented by $\langle\sigma\rangle$ and $x\langle\sigma\rangle x^{-1}$, with normalizers $C_0\times\langle\sigma\rangle$ and its $x$-conjugate. This proves LM4 D.69, including its integral conclusion.

statement: The quartic multiplier assertion of LM4 D.70 Every order-four element of the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group has multiplier globally one. Every finite two-subgroup consequently has multiplier values in the global units $\{1,-1\}$, determined by its dyadic coordinate. No geometric realization or conjugacy assertion is included.

Together with C.16 this proves that every finite subgroup has multiplier image in $\{1,-1\}$, determined by its dyadic coordinate. This independently supplies the transposition inputs LM4 D.36 and D.41.

statement: The proposed cubic lattice admits an invariant unimodular surface form Let $q\equiv1\pmod3$ be an odd prime. The $\mathbb Z_3[C_3]$-module \[ L_q=\mathbb Z_3[\zeta_3]\oplus \mathbb Z_3[C_3]^{\,q-1} \tag{C.24.1} \] admits a $C_3$-invariant unimodular alternating form. All integral fixed vectors have pairings divisible by three. This module is realized by the homology of a geometric order-three action on a closed surface of genus $(3q-1)/2$. Thus a contradiction based solely on the module (C.24.1), its surface form and mod-three isotropy of integral fixed characters cannot exclude a scalar cubic torus coordinate. This is an algebraic limitation of that approach, not a realization of such a torus coordinate.
depends_on: explicit integral matrices and equivariant handle construction
answers: C.3: limitation of quartic-style linear obstruction
notes: No existence of a scalar cubic torus action is asserted; only linear data and a filled-surface realization.

statement: A free-factor route would settle the actual fixed kernel In the notation of C.12, if the actual other fixed group $B$ is a free profinite factor of $F=\widehat F_2$, then $B\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $K=\ker(\chi|_B)=1$. The abstract projective retract constructed in C.2 is not a free profinite factor of $\widehat F_2$.

notes: The actual fixed group has not been proved to be a free profinite factor.

statement: The scalar cubic existence question in prompt C.3 We have not constructed or excluded an order-three element of the full torus loop-outer group whose multiplier has a nonidentity cubic coordinate. C.16 is specific to the three-cusp structure and does not prove the torus assertion. C.24 explains exactly why replacing the quartic involution in C.22 by the proposed cubic integral module does not yield the same contradiction: the fixed vectors come from norms in regular modules and their pairings vanish modulo three. The module is even geometrically realizable on the filled covering surface, while the needed descent to the original punctured torus with its specified nontrivial multiplier is absent. An additional cyclic-cover attempt has the following precise limit. At a scalar cubic coordinate $q$, an eigencharacter $F\to C_q$ is preserved up to a primitive cube-root scalar, rather than pointwise. The induced order-three action consequently permutes nontrivial deck eigenspaces in orbits of length three. Its commutant is no longer the product of unramified fields with multiplicity one used in C.16; the resulting permutation blocks themselves have order three. Thus absence of a nontrivial cubic root in an unramified triadic field does not exclude this different semilinear action. The finite Frobenius quotients proposed in LM4 D.71 and D.73 would impose stronger full-group constraints; without a separate proof that those constraints are incompatible, or a construction of a compatible full action, they do not answer this row.
depends_on: C.16; C.24; exact semilinear deck distinction
notes: Full versus pro-p comparison maps retained.

statement: Mixed-sign diagonal power involutions fail the full torus cusp test For $u\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$ with $u^2=1$, the continuous automorphism \[ \alpha_u:\widehat F(x,y)\longrightarrow\widehat F(x,y), \qquad x\longmapsto x^u,\quad y\longmapsto y^{-u} \tag{C.27.1} \] has order two and determinant $-1$ on full abelianization. It preserves the torus cusp $[x,y]$ up to conjugacy and the power $-1$ if and only if $u=1$ or $u=-1$ globally. In these two cases it is a standard reflection and its noncusp fixed group is $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$. Every pro-$p$ image of (C.27.1) is a standard reflection, including when the full cusp assertion fails. Thus this family gives an explicit mixed-prime obstruction to one natural attempted construction in prompt C.2. It does not classify general negative torus involutions.

statement: Self-centralizing sections for every pure negative sphere action Let $n\geq2$, and let \[ F_n=\widehat{\pi_1(S_{0,n+1})} =\widehat F(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\qquad x_{n+1}=(x_1\cdots x_n)^{-1}. \] Suppose an outer involution preserves each of the $n+1$ peripheral conjugacy classes and sends each $x_j$ to a conjugate of $x_j^{-1}$. In its centre-free extension $1\to F_n\to E\to C_2\to1$, there are exactly $n+1$ $F_n$-conjugacy classes of sections. Every section $S$ satisfies \[ C_{F_n}(S)=1. \tag{C.28.1} \] In particular every genuine involutory representative has trivial fixed subgroup. The assertion concerns the full profinite group, not only its pro-$2$ quotient. More generally, let an involution act compatibly on the full profinite pure mapping class groups of the punctured spheres in a forgetful tower, preserving the individual peripheral classes of each point-pushing kernel with exponent $-1$. Its fixed subgroup in every group of this tower is trivial. The same holds in the pure braid tower, provided the two-strand group is inverted. In particular, the actual action of any multiplier-$-1$ involution of $\widehat{GT}$ on a pure braid group has trivial fixed subgroup.

statement: A full boundary test for automorphisms Let $S$ be a connected compact oriented surface with $m\geq1$ boundary components and negative Euler characteristic. Let $F=\widehat{\pi_1(S)}$ be its full profinite fundamental group and let $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ be its positively oriented boundary generators, based by chosen arcs. Suppose a continuous endomorphism $\varphi:F\to F$ satisfies \[ \varphi(c_j)=g_jc_{\sigma(j)}^{\mu_j}g_j^{-1} \quad(1\leq j\leq m), \qquad \sigma\in\mathfrak S_m,\quad \mu_j\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\quad g_j\in F. \] Then $\varphi$ is an automorphism. If $m\geq2$, its exponents $\mu_j$ are necessarily equal. In particular, for the full profinite pants group, a substitution \[ x\longmapsto x^\mu,\qquad y\longmapsto u^{-1}y^\mu u \] with $\mu\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$ is an automorphism as soon as $x^\mu u^{-1}y^\mu u$ is conjugate to $(xy)^\mu$. No separate full-generation hypothesis is needed.

statement: Unit hexagon solutions are full automorphisms Let $F=\widehat F(x,y)$, put $z=(xy)^{-1}$, and let $\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$ and $f\in F'$. In particular no separate invertibility hypothesis is needed for a unit pair satisfying these two full equations. If it also satisfies the full pentagon, it belongs to the full Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group, including its unit requirement.

statement: The paired involution has exactly the peripheral coinvariant kernel Retain \(\alpha,u,v\), and \(\tau=\alpha v\) from C.37, and put \(z=(xy)^{-1}\). statement: The correctly normalized third cusp holds in every symmetric-four quotient Let \(\alpha=(-1,f)\) be an involution of the full \(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\), and let \(u\in F'\) be its canonical full R1 word. statement: An explicit first relation-module bound for the canonical word Let $F=\widehat F(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, let $c(x_i)=x_i^{-1}$, and let $q:F\to Q$ be a finite quotient with $c$-stable kernel $U$. statement: One dyadic homology step determines the canonical head Let $F$ be a finitely generated free profinite group, let $\sigma$ be an involution, and suppose every involution of $E=F\rtimes_\sigma C_2$ has centralizer exactly its order-two subgroup. If $U\trianglelefteq F$ is open and $\sigma$-stable, then \[ C_{F/\Phi_2(U)}(\sigma)\longrightarrow F/U \quad\hbox{has trivial image}. \tag{C.42.1} \] More precisely, two actual sections of $U\rtimes_\sigma C_2$ that are conjugate modulo $\Phi_2(U)$ are already $U$-conjugate. The hypotheses hold for every pure negative sphere action in C.28, in particular for every full negative pants involution. For the actual rank-two canonical equation $u=f\alpha(u)$, all solutions of its induced equation in $F/\Phi_2(U)$ have the same image in $F/U$, namely the image of the unique full word $u$. Thus that head value is determined by finite data at this explicit relative level. This does not compute an unspecified existential parameter $f$, prove generation, or settle the third cusp.

statement: The invariant metric and compact-core collapse The function \[ d_Q(u,v)=\sup_{q\in Q}d(qu,qv) \] is a bounded $Q$-invariant metric inducing the original topology on $O$. If $A,B\subset O$ are compact, $a_j\in A$, and $q_ja_j\to z\in\partial\overline D$, then $q_jB\to\{z\}$ uniformly in the original metric.

The exact $C_0$ image and compact-parameter criterion For $h\in C_{\operatorname{Homeo}(O)}(Q)$ define \[ \delta_h(\pi u)=d_Q(hu,u),\qquad V=\{h\in C_{\operatorname{Homeo}(O)}(Q):\delta_h\in C_0(N)\}. \] Here $C_0(N)$ consists of continuous functions vanishing uniformly outside compact subsets. Restriction $C\to V$ and extension by the identity on $\partial\overline D$ are inverse isometric topological group isomorphisms, for the sums of the uniform distances of maps and inverses. For a compact metrizable parameter space $P$, an equivariant family $h_s$ with continuous evaluation $P\times O\to O$ extends jointly to the closed disk if and only if \begin{equation}\label{eq:DE-tail} \forall\epsilon>0\ \exists K\Subset N:\quad \sup_{s\in P,\,\pi u\notin K}d_Q(h_su,u)<\epsilon. \end{equation} Joint continuity of the extended inverse family follows as well. This proves LM4 C.88 with its stated hypotheses.

Pointed descent, its image, and its stronger topology Let \[ I_p=\operatorname{Homeo}(N\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}}p)_0 \] denote the identity path component in the compact-open topology on maps and inverses. Every $a\in F$ descends to $I_p$. Every $b\in I_p$ has a unique lift $\lambda(b):O\to O$ fixing $x$, and that lift commutes with every element of $Q$. Define \[ B_p=\{b\in I_p:\delta_{\lambda(b)}\in C_0(N)\}. \] Descent gives a group isomorphism $F\to B_p$ and an isometry if $B_p$ is given the metric \begin{align*} d^{\uparrow}(b,c)={}&\sup_{u\in O}d_Q(\lambda(b)u,\lambda(c)u)\\ &+\sup_{u\in O}d_Q(\lambda(b)^{-1}u,\lambda(c)^{-1}u). \end{align*} For compact parameter spaces, continuity in this metric is exactly compact-open continuity downstairs together with \eqref{eq:DE-tail} for the actual pointed lifts. This proves LM4 C.92, including its distinction between the two topologies.

Evaluation has a global section in the original topology For every quotient $N$ under consideration, compact or noncompact, there is a continuous map $s:O\to C$ with $s(y)x=y$ and $s(x)=1$. Consequently \[ C\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }O\times F,\qquad a\longmapsto\bigl(ax,s(ax)^{-1}a\bigr) \] is a homeomorphism, with inverse $(y,f)\mapsto s(y)f$. In particular $\pi_j(F,1)\to\pi_j(C,1)$ is an isomorphism for all $j\geq1$.

The compact quotient case is contractible If $N$ is compact, $C$ admits a continuous contraction to $1$ fixing $1$ throughout. This proves both LM4 C.90 and LM4 C.91, including the torus and Klein-bottle quotients.

Compact-open convergence does not control the lifted tail There are operators satisfying all the hypotheses above, with $N=S^1\times\mathbb R$, and $b_R\in B_p$ converging to $1$ in $I_p$ while $d^{\uparrow}(b_R,1)>2/5$ for every $R\geq2$.

statement: Families with one compact quotient support fill Let $a:S^m\to C$ be a based sphere family, $m\geq1$, and suppose that one compact set $K\Subset N$ satisfies $a_\xi(u)=u$ whenever $\pi u\notin K$. Then $a$ has a based null-homotopy in $C$ with one compact quotient support, and hence with a uniform tail.

The trivial operator case and the compact-open exception If $Q=1$, the whole group $C$ and every point stabilizer $F$ are contractible in their actual topology, even though the identity component of $\operatorname{Homeo}(\mathbb R^2\mathbin{\mathrm{rel}}0)$ in the interior compact-open topology has homotopy type $S^1$.

The arbitrary noncompact quotient uniform-tail deformation Assume the quotient $N$ is noncompact. Let $P$ be a compact metrizable space and $a:P\to F$ a continuous map. Does $a$ admit a homotopy to the constant identity that is continuous in the metric $d^{\uparrow}$? The relative version for a prescribed subset on which $a=1$ is also undecided here. In particular we have not proved or refuted $\pi_1(C,1)=0$ in this generality. The precise missing estimate is \eqref{eq:DE-tail} uniformly in $(s,t)\in P\times[0,1]$. The unqualified compact-open contraction of a pointed noncompact surface does not supply it, as D.6 makes concrete. A sufficient constructive route is a deformation of every based sphere family to one with common compact quotient support, preserving this estimate; D.7 would then finish the sphere. No such cutoff has been constructed for an arbitrary $d_Q$. We checked the later uniform-deformation literature as well. Yagasaki's covering-space theorem has a compact base \cite[Theorem 1.1]{DE_Yagasaki2014}. Its end theorem assumes specified Euclidean ends. The later end theorem requires finitely many isolated proper product ends with the stated end-deformation property \cite[Theorem 1.3]{DE_Yagasaki2018}. Neither hypothesis follows from the present data. In particular the bounded metric $d_Q$ need not be a proper end metric, and no comparison transferring the needed deformation to $d^{\uparrow}$ has been proved. We also considered equivariant deformations of a null lifted triangulation. Its pointwise skeleton stabilizer contracts. The family of skeleton embeddings still requires a deformation with the same uniform control. The escaping sequence in D.6 has not been turned into a nontrivial loop; presenting it as one would be an error.
notes: Open: no uniform-tail contraction or nontrivial loop obtained; compact-open contraction does not suffice.

statement: Arbitrary-frontier descent in the exact comparison Let $U$ be a simply connected open orbit in the original surface. The prime-end disk need not map continuously onto its closure. When the interior identification has such an extension, its boundary map may fail to be injective. We have not proved that an intrinsic centralizer filling can be chosen to extend over every such original frontier, with jointly continuous inverses. An interior conjugacy alone does not suffice. One must retain all original approach limits and prescribed frontier values; a boundary equivalence relation describes only the cases where a continuous boundary map exists. This is the arbitrary-frontier descent obligation listed in LM4 C.12.

statement: Nonfixed-frontier pasting and infinitely many orbit types The remaining LM4 C.12 comparison requires simultaneous fillings on all open orbits agreeing with a deforming, possibly nonfixed, nonopen locus, including infinitely many operator-inequivalent remaining components and accumulation outside the treated closed sets. We have not proved or refuted this assertion. The missing conditions are (i) existence of mutually compatible restrictions on every common frontier, (ii) extension of these restrictions over the incident open orbits, and (iii) uniform control of both maps and inverses across arbitrary accumulating families. D.2 controls one original disk with fixed boundary and does not supply these three comparisons.

statement: The universal admissible level-zero kernel For an admissible punctured surface, with actual homeomorphism group $A$, a strict action $u:\Gamma\to A$, and $H=u(\Gamma)$, the unresolved comparison of LM4 C.12 is injectivity of \[ \pi_1(C_A(H),1)\longrightarrow\pi_1(A,1)^\Gamma. \] For hyperbolic finite-type surfaces the target is zero, so the question is whether every based centralizer loop contracts in the centralizer. For the plane, annulus, and torus the respective targets are the invariant subgroups of $\mathbb Z$, $\mathbb Z$, and $\mathbb Z^2$.
