statement: Planar filling hulls preserve the invariant diameter bound Choose closed-disk coordinates in which $d$ is Euclidean, and retain $d_Q(u,v)=\sup_q|qu-qv|$. This changes neither the actual group topology nor its $C_0$ tail condition. For a nonempty compact $A\subset O$, let $\operatorname{Fill}(A)$ be $A$ together with all relatively compact components of $O\setminus A$. Then \[ q\operatorname{Fill}(A)=\operatorname{Fill}(qA),\qquad \operatorname{diam}_{d_Q}\operatorname{Fill}(A) =\operatorname{diam}_{d_Q}(A). \] Moreover, if $A\subset B_{d_Q}(x,r)$ is compact, then $\operatorname{Fill}(A)\subset B_{d_Q}(x,r)$. Every connected component of a $d_Q$-ball is a simply connected open planar domain. In particular every loop contained in one such ball has a filling in that same ball.
notes: Ball components simply connected; does not supply controlled parametric ambient isotopy.

statement: An inner-diameter metric retaining every based sphere family Inner-diameter metrics also occur in \cite[Definition 2.2]{DE_Fabel1998}. With the invariant metric in D.13, put \[ \rho(u,v)=\inf\{\operatorname{diam}_{d_Q}(\alpha): \alpha\subset O\text{ is an arc joining }u\text{ to }v\}. \] Then $\rho$ is a bounded $Q$-invariant metric inducing the original interior topology, and $d_Q\leq\rho$. Its open balls are path connected. If $U(u,r)$ is the component of $B_{d_Q}(u,r)$ containing $u$, then $U(u,r)$ is an open topological disk and \[ B_\rho(u,r)\subset U(u,r)\subset B_\rho(u,2r). \] Every map $S^j\to B_\rho(u,r)$, $j\geq1$, is null-homotopic in $B_\rho(u,2r)$. Let $F^\rho\subset F$ consist of maps whose lift displacement for $\rho$ belongs to $C_0(N)$, equipped with the uniform $\rho$ topology on maps and inverses. Every based continuous family $P\to F$ from a compact, connected, locally path-connected metric space is also a continuous family into $F^\rho$, with a uniform $\rho$ tail. Consequently inclusion $F^\rho\to F$ induces isomorphisms on every positive based homotopy group. This reduces the sphere-family part of D.9 to a metric with connected balls and the displayed uniform filling bound; it does not prove the ambient deformation.
answers: D.2 controlled metric reduction for positive homotopy groups
notes: Bρ(u,r) lies in an open disk U(u,r) inside Bρ(u,2r); positive based homotopy groups are preserved. Controlled equivariant ambient isotopy remains unproved.

statement: Arbitrary simply connected frontiers with trivial operators Let $U\subset S^2$ be a simply connected open domain whose complement $K$ contains at least two points. Give \[ H_U=\{h\in\operatorname{Homeo}^+(S^2):h|_K=1_K\} \] the original uniform topology on maps and inverses. Then $H_U$ is homeomorphic to the separable Hilbert space $\ell^2$ and has an identity-fixed contraction. In particular every compact family in this group contracts with joint continuity on the original sphere, even when $\partial U$ is not locally connected. This settles the trivial-operator case of the arbitrary-frontier obligation. It does not assert an equivariant contraction for nontrivial operators.
answers: D.3 arbitrary-frontier trivial-operator subcase;LM4 C.67 extension
notes: Original sphere-uniform topology; no local connectedness required; complement must be nondegenerate. No equivariant contraction asserted.

statement: An obstruction to global equivariant compression Suppose a continuous $Q$-equivariant map $e:O\to O$ has image contained in $\pi^{-1}(S)$ for some compact connected subsurface $S\subset N$. Then $Q$ is finitely generated. In particular, when $Q$ is infinitely generated, there is no $Q$-equivariant embedding that compresses all of $O$ over one compact quotient core. This rules out that direct adaptation of the compression step of D.15; it does not refute D.9.
depends_on: Covering endpoint identification;finite generation of compact-surface groups
answers: D.2 obstruction to the direct Fabel compression method
notes: Only a method obstruction: a Q-equivariant map into the preimage of a compact quotient core forces Q finitely generated. Does not refute the group contraction.

statement: Joint equivariant map fillings with a uniform quotient tail Let $P$ be a compact connected locally path-connected metric space, and let $a:P\to F$ be continuous and based at the identity. Put $A=\{s\in P:a_s=1\}$. There is a jointly continuous map \[ E:P\times[0,1]\times\overline D\longrightarrow\overline D \] such that $E_{s,0}=a_s$, $E_{s,1}=1$, and $E_{s,t}=1$ for $s\in A$. Every $E_{s,t}$ fixes the original boundary and $x$, maps $O$ into $O$, and commutes there with $Q$. Moreover there is a positive function $\eta\in C_0(N)$ such that \[ \rho(E_{s,t}(v),v)\leq128\eta(\pi v) \quad(s\in P, t\in[0,1], v\in O). \] Thus the construction retains the uniform quotient tail and joint continuity in the evaluated point. The construction does not preserve injectivity. In particular this statement does not give a filling in $F$.
answers: Part D.2 joint evaluated-point homotopy step; not ambient homeomorphism filling
notes: Explicit displacement bound 128 eta; triangulated quotient and Tietze extension inside controlled open-disk carriers. Injectivity of intermediate maps is not proved; D.9 remains Open.

statement: The compact real-type injection of LM6 C.13 For $g\geq2$, the topological types of orientation-reversing involutions of $S_g$ inject into conjugacy classes in $\operatorname{Out}(\widehat{\pi_1(S_g)})$. They consequently inject into conjugacy classes in $Q_g^{\pm}$ and $P_g^{\pm}$. For genus three the six types are \[ (r,a)=(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(2,0),(4,0). \tag{E.1.1} \]
depends_on: BZ 2025 Theorem A at p=2; surface goodness; oval homology
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: Marked incidence and the simultaneous orientation in LM6 C.14 The injection of E.1 holds for individually labelled real markings, and for unordered markings allowing nonreal conjugate pairs. A peripheral isomorphism of the completed real surface extensions recovers the cyclic incidence of real marked points on each oval. For dividing surfaces, the cyclic orders on labelled marked ovals are identified only by their simultaneous reversal.
depends_on: E.1; full peripheral maps; finite graph covers
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The exact nonabelian-cohomology fibre of LM6 C.15 Let $1\to K\to P^{\pm}\xrightarrow{q}Q^{\pm}\to1$ be a continuous exact sequence of profinite groups with compatible orientation characters, with $K\leq P$ their positive kernel. Fix an orientation-reversing involution $\tau\in P^{\pm}$ and put $\alpha=\operatorname{Ad}(\tau)$ and $\bar\tau=q(\tau)$. For $k\in K$ satisfying $k\alpha(k)=1$, identify cocycles by $k\sim b k\alpha(b)^{-1}$, $b\in K$. Then \begin{align} q(g)\star[k]&=[gk\alpha(g)^{-1}],\notag\\ \{\text{$P$-classes over }[\bar\tau]\} &\cong C_Q(\bar\tau)\backslash H^1(C_2,K), \tag{E.3.1}\\ 1\longrightarrow K^{k\tau}\longrightarrow C_P(k\tau) &\xrightarrow{q} \operatorname{Stab}_{C_Q(\bar\tau)}([k]) \longrightarrow1 . \tag{E.3.2} \end{align} Here $g\in P$ is any lift of the indicated quotient-centralizer element. The action need not fix the class of the trivial cocycle.
notes: Quotient-centralizer action may move the trivial cocycle class; D8 example checked.

statement: The hyperelliptic comparison of LM6 C.16 uses only the element theorem Fix a hyperelliptic involution $\iota\in\Gamma_3$, and put $H^{\pm}=C_{\Gamma_3^{\pm}}(\iota)$ and $H=H^{\pm}\cap\Gamma_3$. The natural map $\widehat{H^{\pm}}\to P_3^{\pm}$ is injective, with image $\overline{H^{\pm}}$. Each orientation-reversing involution in this image is $\overline H$-conjugate to a discrete one. For such a discrete involution $\tau$, \[ C_{P_3}(\tau)\cap\overline H =\overline{C_H(\tau)}. \tag{E.4.1} \] Each of the six types in (E.1.1) has a representative in $H^{\pm}$. No centralizer equality for a nonsolvable finite subgroup is used in these assertions.
depends_on: Boggi 2024 Theorem 7.1; BZ 2025 Theorem A at p=2
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The five oval centralizers of LM6 C.17 Let $\tau\in\Gamma_3^{\pm}$ be a real involution with $r>0$, and put $C=C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau)$. The restriction of $q$ is an isomorphism \[ \overline C^{\,P_3}\xrightarrow{\sim} C_{Q_3}(\bar\tau)=\overline C^{\,Q_3},\qquad C_{P_3}(\tau)=K_c^\tau\rtimes\overline C^{\,P_3}. \tag{E.5.1} \] For these five types the quotient-centralizer action of E.3 fixes the trivial cohomology class. Formula (E.5.1) does not compute $K_c^\tau$.
depends_on: E.2; Boggi 2014 Theorem 4.5; Boggi 2020 genus ≤2 comparison; BZ element theorem
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The free real type has the exact comparison of LM6 C.18 For the fixed-point-free genus-three involution $\tau$, put $N_4=S_3/\tau$, $E=\widehat{\pi_1(N_4)}$, and $\Pi=\widehat{\pi_1(S_3)}$. Let $\operatorname{Aut}_{Q}(E;\Pi)$ be the continuous automorphisms preserving $\Pi$ whose restrictions have outer class in $Q_3^{\pm}$. Then \[ \mathcal A:=\operatorname{Aut}_{Q}(E;\Pi)/\operatorname{Inn}(E) \cong C_{Q_3^{\pm}}(\bar\tau)/\langle\bar\tau\rangle \cong C_{Q_3}(\bar\tau). \tag{E.6.1} \] Under this homeomorphism the closure of $\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)$ equals the closure of $C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau)$ in $Q_3$. Equality of this closure with $\mathcal A$ remains a density question.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The obstruction to a hyperelliptic reduction in LM6 C.19 For the positive lift $j:\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)\cong C_{\Gamma_3}(\tau)$ and every finite-index subgroup $H\leq\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)$, the centralizer $C_{\Gamma_3}(j(H))$ has no nonidentity finite-order element. In particular $j(H)$ is never contained in a hyperelliptic centralizer, and the standard hyperelliptic subgroup of $\operatorname{Mod}(N_4)$ has infinite index.
depends_on: Farb–Margalit Propositions 2.3, 3.20 and Lemma 3.17; signed pants lifts
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: Finite quotients retain the entire fixed group and nonabelian cohomology Let a finite group $C_2=\langle\tau\rangle$ act continuously on a profinite group $K$, and let $N$ range over its open normal $\tau$-invariant subgroups. There are natural homeomorphisms \[ K^\tau\cong\varprojlim_N(K/N)^\tau, \qquad H^1(C_2,K)\cong\varprojlim_N H^1(C_2,K/N). \tag{E.8.1} \] The cohomology set is given the quotient topology of its compact cocycle space. Neither the maps to individual finite fixed groups nor the finite cohomology transition maps are asserted to be surjective.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The fixed congruence kernel is the fibre of oval stabilizers For one of the five oval types in E.5, let $A$ be its oval multicurve and $L=\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma_3}(A)$. Use E.5 to regard $\widehat L$ as a closed subgroup of $P_3$ mapping isomorphically onto $(Q_3)_A$. Then the fibre over the identity coset of the continuous map \[ P_3/\widehat L\longrightarrow Q_3/(Q_3)_A \] is naturally the profinite set $K_c$. Its $\tau$-fixed subset is naturally $K_c^\tau$.
depends_on: E.5; fibre of the multicurve-stabilizer map
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The six congruence-kernel computations in prompt E.1 For each type (E.1.1), determine $K_c^\tau$ and the nonabelian pointed set $H^1(C_2,K_c)$ for $\operatorname{Ad}(\tau)$. E.3 gives the exact class and centralizer formula after these groups and sets are known; E.5 supplies its quotient-centralizer term for the five oval types. For $(0,1)$ the density question in E.6 remains an additional unresolved term. The current state is \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} (r,a)&C_{Q_3}(\bar\tau)&K_c^\tau&H^1(C_2,K_c)\\\hline (0,1)&\mathcal A\text{ of E.6}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}\\ (1,1)&\overline C^{\,Q_3}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}\\ (2,1)&\overline C^{\,Q_3}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}\\ (3,1)&\overline C^{\,Q_3}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}\\ (2,0)&\overline C^{\,Q_3}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}\\ (4,0)&\overline C^{\,Q_3}&\text{uncomputed}&\text{uncomputed}. \end{array} \tag{E.10.1} \] The existence of six geometric classes is proved, and their distinctness persists in both completions; a classification of all profinite classes does not follow. E.8 gives exact inverse-limit computations but no presentation of the required finite quotients of $K_c$. E.9 identifies a separate geometric fixed-fibre problem. The hyperelliptic route settles the intersection in E.4; E.7 rules out extending that route to the free type by passing to a finite-index nonorientable mapping class subgroup. No vanishing of the genus-three congruence kernel is assumed. The contemporary source \cite[Problem~19 and the following paragraph]{CEAndrewHenselHughesWade2026} explicitly records that the mapping class congruence subgroup problem remains open in genus at least three.
notes: Full profinite groups unless explicitly designated pro-p or procongruence.

statement: The holomorphic classification of five-point configurations The possible full holomorphic automorphism groups are \[ 1,\quad C_2,\quad C_4,\quad D_3,\quad D_5. \] If the maximum order $\nu$ of a nonidentity holomorphic automorphism is $5$, $4$, or $3$, there is exactly one isomorphism class, respectively \[ \mu_5,\qquad\{\infty\}\cup\mu_4, \qquad\{0,\infty\}\cup\mu_3. \] Their full groups are $D_5,C_4,D_3$. The labeled structures are, respectively, an unoriented pentagon, a distinguished point with an oriented square on the other four points, and a three-set together with its two-element orientation torsor. These assertions verify the holomorphic classification on cote 148, scan 34, handwritten p.~1.

The one-parameter involution locus and the square and tetrahedron cases Every five-point configuration with a nontrivial holomorphic involution can be written \[ K_t=\{\infty,1,-1,t,-t\},\qquad t\ne0,\ \ t^2\ne1. \] For a configuration with the involution specified, its isomorphism class is determined by \[ \lambda=t^2,\qquad\beta=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\in\mathbb C\setminus\{2\}. \] The full group is $C_2$ except at \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} \beta&-2&-10/3&18\\\hline \operatorname{Aut}^+(K_t)&C_4&D_3&D_5. \end{array} \] A harmonic four-set together with a fixed point of one of its fixed-point-free involutions gives $\beta=-2$ or $34$. The second case has full group $C_2$; it is neither the pentagonal nor the square-pyramidal case. An equianharmonic four-set with such a fixed point gives $\beta=-14$ and full group $C_2$. These formulas complete the calculation begun and then crossed out on cote 148, scan 35, handwritten p.~2, and answer its question about adding an edge midpoint to a spherical square.

Every finite antiholomorphic automorphism preserving five marks has order two The inference in cote 148, scan 35, handwritten p.~2, that an even-order antiholomorphic automorphism preserving five points must fix a marked point and therefore have order two is false. The exact possible orders of antiholomorphic automorphisms of five-point configurations are $2,6,10$.
notes: Original scan inspected: explicit anti-Mobius order6 and order10 counterexamples; exact code attached.

statement: Real involutions, dimensions, and their exact relation to the symmetric square An antiholomorphic \emph{involution} preserving five marked points has a fixed circle and fixes exactly $r=1,3,$ or $5$ of the marks. Each of these three spaces of real pairs $(\mathbb P^1,K,\sigma)$ has real dimension two. The examples in cote 148, scan 36, handwritten p.~3, are valid: the pentagonal configuration has an $r=5$ real structure, the triangular bipyramid has an $r=3$ structure, and the square pyramid has an $r=1$ structure. These examples are not exclusive to the indicated type.

The generic real involution locus For $K_t$ of E.31 with full positive group $C_2$, a real structure exists exactly when $\beta$ is real. The full extended group is then $C_2\times C_2$, and the fixed-mark counts of its two negative involutions are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{range of }\beta&\text{counts}\\\hline \beta>2&\{5,1\}\\ \beta<-2&\{3,3\}\\ -2<\beta<2&\{1,1\}. \end{array} \] The enhanced values in E.31 are omitted from the indicated ranges.

Reflection section classes for five punctures Let $U=\mathbb P^1\setminus K$ and let $\sigma$ be a real involution fixing $r\in\{1,3,5\}$ marks. Put $m=(5-r)/2$. Its discrete orbifold extension is \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_1(U)\longrightarrow E_\sigma\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow1, \qquad E_\sigma\cong\Bigl(\mathop{*}_{j=1}^{r}C_2\Bigr)*F_m. \] The sign map is nontrivial on each $C_2$ factor and trivial on $F_m$. It has exactly $r$ conjugacy classes of sections under $\pi_1(U)$, one for each component of $U^\sigma$; every section has trivial fixed subgroup in $\pi_1(U)$. This verifies the five-point instances of LM4 B.4 and B.5.

The twenty finite-subgroup classes in type $(0,5)$ The discrete extended mapping class group of a sphere with five unordered punctures has exactly twenty conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, including the trivial group. Seven preserve orientation and thirteen have nontrivial sign. In the following table, the last column lists the fixed-mark counts of all negative involutions, with multiplicity; an empty entry means there are none. \begin{center}\small \begin{tabular}{c|r|c|l} $G$&$|G|$&$G^+$&\text{negative involutions}\\\hline $1$&1&$1$&\\ $C_2$&2&$C_2$&\\ $C_3$&3&$C_3$&\\ $C_4$&4&$C_4$&\\ $C_5$&5&$C_5$&\\ $D_3$&6&$D_3$&\\ $D_5$&10&$D_5$&\\\hline $C_2$&2&$1$&$5$\\ $C_2$&2&$1$&$3$\\ $C_2$&2&$1$&$1$\\ $C_2\times C_2$&4&$C_2$&$5,1$\\ $C_2\times C_2$&4&$C_2$&$3,3$\\ $C_2\times C_2$&4&$C_2$&$1,1$\\ $C_6$&6&$C_3$&$3$\\ $D_3$&6&$C_3$&$3,3,3$\\ $D_4$&8&$C_4$&$1,1,3,3$\\ $C_{10}$&10&$C_5$&$5$\\ $D_5$&10&$C_5$&$1,1,1,1,1$\\ $D_3\times C_2$&12&$D_3$&$3,3,3,3$\\ $D_5\times C_2$&20&$D_5$&$1,1,1,1,1,5$ \end{tabular} \end{center} Thus the type $(0,5)$ total in LM4 B.26 is correct, although it must not be identified with the number of full automorphism groups of individual complex configurations.
notes: 20=7 positive+13 mixed; exact S5 x C2 models pairwise nonconjugate.

statement: The nine vertex families contain 542 labeled objects The vertex structures displayed in cote 148, scan 31, have the following cardinalities and are each one transitive $S_5$-set: \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r} \text{type}&\text{stabilizer order}&\text{cardinality}\\\hline I_{10}&10&12\\ I_6&6&20\\ I_4&4&30\\ II_2&2&60\\ II'_2&2&60\\ II_1&1&120\\ III_2&2&60\\ III_1&1&120\\ III'_2&2&60 \end{array} \] Their disjoint union has $542$ objects in nine $S_5$-orbits.

statement: The fourteen arrow families form fourteen $S_5$-orbits For the arrow families and local degrees displayed in cote 148, scans 31 and 33, the sizes are \[ 60,120;\quad60,120,60,60,120;\quad 120,120,120,120,360,120,60. \] They sum to $1620$. They cannot form fourteen $S_5$-orbits. The size-$360$ family from $III_1$ to $II_1$ has three free $S_5$-orbits, and the indicated remaining families give thirteen orbits. The resulting count is sixteen, with sizes $5\cdot60+11\cdot120$.

statement: The undecorated square pyramid has no real structure If the phrase on cote 148, scan 31, excluding $I_4$ from the real structures is interpreted as a statement about the undecorated five-point complex configuration, it is false. For $K=\{\infty,1,i,-1,-i\}$, complex conjugation preserves $K$, and its full extended automorphism group is $D_4$ of order eight.

statement: The stable-tree counts on scan 36 For five labeled marks, the stable genus-zero dual trees with zero, one, and two edges have respectively $1,10,15$ combinatorial types. The corresponding decorated counts written at the bottom of cote 148, scan 36, are $12$ in the pentagonal top type, $60$ and $120$ for the two indicated one-edge decorations, and $60$ for the indicated two-edge decoration. LM4 D.28 holds for the full pure three-cusp group Let \(p\) be a prime and \(\rho:C_p\to\mathcal P\) a continuous homomorphism whose multiplier has \(p\)-component one. Let \(\alpha\) be the unique normalized actual representative of the image of a named generator, and set \[ E=F\rtimes_\alpha C_p,\qquad S=\{1\}\times C_p,\qquad C=C_F(S). \] There is one \(F\)-conjugacy class of sections of \(E\to C_p\). Each of the three peripheral normalizers contains a section, and inclusion induces \[ C^{(p)}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{(p)}. \] Here \(C^{(p)}\) is the maximal pro-\(p\) quotient of the actual full fixed subgroup. The statement is valid for \(\mathcal P\), not merely for \(\widehat{GT}_0\).
notes: Independent argument uses normalization, Magnus, cusp norms and full-profinite Brown restriction; no GT symmetry or R1 conclusion is used.

statement: The normalized section and the independent Magnus lemma remove the citation cycle The pure peripheral outer group \(\mathcal P\) has a unique normalized homomorphic section into \(\operatorname{Aut}(F)\) of the form \[ x\longmapsto x^\lambda, \qquad y\longmapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f, \qquad f\in F'. \] For every prime \(p\), a finite-order continuous automorphism of a finitely generated free pro-\(p\) group which is identity on integral abelianization is identity. This lemma is independent of LM4 D.25's final conclusion and of LM4 D.32.
answers: E.3: remove LM4 D.25-D.32 citation cycle
notes: Integral homogeneous leading terms are torsion-free; independent of the final R1-dependent conclusion of LM4 D.25. Explicit acyclic dependency order recorded.

statement: The precise Herfort--Ribes citation for the free peripheral reduction For \(F=\widehat F(x,y)\), each peripheral cyclic group \(L=\overline{\langle u\rangle}\), where \(u=x,y,(xy)^{-1}\), is malnormal, and \[ N_F(L)=L, \qquad C_F(u^a)=L \quad(0\ne a\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \] The analogous statements hold in \(F^{(p)}\), with \(0\ne a\in\mathbb Z_p\). The precise source in the free-factor reduction of LM4 A.7 is Herfort--Ribes (1985), \emph{Theorem B'}, Section~4, printed page~159.\cite{A_HR1985}
notes: Full and pro-p formations both included. Does not replace the distinct commensurator theorem for the nonprimitive boundary of a once-punctured surface.
